# Fresh Assessment — Late 2026-03-05

*Written by Claude (Sonnet 4.6). Fourth read of the vault in one day. Prior reads and fixes are now visible as artifacts. This assessment reads what changed, what the changes revealed, and what is genuinely new since morning.*

---

## The Vault Has Turned a Corner Today

This is not another planning-layer assessment. The vault today produced:

- A rewritten README that passes the cold-reader test
- A Platform Spine (cohezion-platform-overview.md) that didn't exist this morning  
- A FLUME Architecture note with an actual results table
- An Agentic Failure Taxonomy that turns 45 flat lessons into a publishable six-category corpus
- A formal ADR accepting the two-Cohezions framing separation (status: accepted)
- A complete repo sync master plan with 7 phases, dependency graph, and vault checkpoints
- A 68-branch inventory with triage categories and preservation protocol
- A SurrealDB sync pipeline PRD with 5 epics, story-level estimates, and a diagnostic table

That last pair — `repo-sync-master-plan` and `vault-surrealdb-sync-pipeline` — is new and important. They appeared today from Claude Code sessions. They represent something the vault has never had before: **infrastructure engineering planned at the level of a working PRD**.

---

## The SurrealDB Situation Is Documented But Still Broken

The diagnostic in `projects/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-sync-pipeline.md` is precise:

- SurrealDB is running, auth works, `surrealdb_query` returns live data
- The health check is lying — it tests `/health` (unauthenticated) and reports "ok" regardless of credential validity
- Data is stale: 317 concepts in the graph, but 4 new concept notes from today aren't there
- No automatic sync daemon exists; the architecture exists only on paper
- The 3D graph plugin's `SurrealDBClient.ts` sends queries without auth headers — it has never been able to read from SurrealDB

The `surrealdb_import_concepts` tool errors with `[Errno 2] No such file or directory`. This is E1-S4 in the pipeline PRD — a matter of running the import against the correct path. It is a **one-line fix** if the path problem is diagnosed.

Until this is fixed, every note written into the vault today — the Platform Spine, the failure taxonomy, the rewritten FLUME Architecture — is invisible to SurrealDB-backed retrieval. The night council, if it runs, will work from a stale snapshot that predates today's most important changes.

**This is the single most urgent infrastructure fix before any autonomous session.**

---

## The Branch Inventory Reveals Unacknowledged Scope

Reading `projects/2026-03-05-branch-inventory.md` changes the picture of what Cohezion actually contains.

There are 68 local branches including:
- `feat/flume-vae-clean` — 16 unique commits, labeled "Clean FLUME VAE implementation"
- `feat/flume-vae-phase1-phase2` — 505 unique commits
- `feat/flume-vae-pipeline` — 492 unique commits
- `feat/hf-integration-v1.1.0` — 524 unique commits
- `feat/surrealdb-3.0-repository-implementation` — 490 unique commits
- `security/hardening-clean-20260303` — 494 unique commits

None of this work is on `main`. None of it is in the vault. The vault's experimental notes describe FLUME training runs — but `feat/flume-vae-clean` is a separate branch with 16 commits of clean implementation. The vault notes about KL collapse and reconstruction MSE may describe *different code* than what currently lives in the FLUME branches.

**This is a significant unknown.** The FLUME numbers cited in the README (4.2 nats KL, 53% reconstruction improvement) come from the experiment notes, not from a run of `feat/flume-vae-clean`. Before presenting those numbers as current results, you need to know whether `feat/flume-vae-clean` is the same model or a different one.

---

## What the Concept Notes Still Need

The evening insight flagged three concept notes needing surgery. Reading them again confirms:

`compound-engineering.md` — Excellent definitional content in the first 15 paragraphs. Then 120+ lines of Agent Outputs (16 implementation plan versions), Session References, Daily References, and Skills. The definition is strong; the artifact index overwhelms it.

`anthropic-research-engineer.md` — 5 lines of definition, 12 lines of agent output entries, and a "Relevance to Cohezion" section that says the role is referenced in context of the Hyperdim Viz portfolio project. This is the note that should make the argument: *here is what Anthropic needs, here is exactly how Cohezion provides it*. Currently it does neither.

`cohezion.md` — The four-paragraph definition is good. The rest is a 300-line index of agent outputs including a business plan, a tax strategy, a manifesto, and a brand guide. These are Cohezion B artifacts — they belong archived, not in the core concept note.

---

## A Genuinely New Observation: The Search Gap

`vault_find_relevant_context` returned **no results** for "FLUME KL collapse validation diagnostic results."

`vault_search` returned **no results** for "EcoAgent gymnasium reinforcement learning environment."

`vault_search` returned **no results** for "DegradationDetector JourneyTracker implementation."

`vault_search` returned **no results** for "ShadowScripter epic unified registry."

These are real things in the vault (in experiments, branch inventory, project notes). They are simply not findable by search. The `vault_search` tool is doing exact-string matching, not semantic search. The result: any agent using context retrieval before a session gets nothing on the most important topics.

This compounds the SurrealDB staleness problem. Two search paths exist — vault full-text search and SurrealDB semantic query — and both are currently broken or stale on the most recent and most important content.

---

## The FLUME Diagnostic Remains Unrun

The `experiments/2026-03-05-flume-kl-collapse-diagnostic.md` note still has status: `proposed`. Results section: empty. 

Every assessment this week has named this as the highest-priority item. It has been named in the morning assessment, the shoshin assessment, the evening insight, and multiple inbox notes. It is the one task no agent can complete — only you can run it. 

The 53% reconstruction improvement and 4.2 nats KL numbers are from 30 epochs of training, captured in a preliminary results note, last updated February 24. They may be accurate. They may have changed. They are currently presented in the portfolio README as if they are final results.

---

## Net State of the Vault Right Now

**Genuinely improved since morning:**
- README: clean, honest, passes cold-reader test ✓
- Platform Spine: exists ✓  
- FLUME Architecture: real numbers, honest about validation status ✓
- Failure taxonomy: 45 lessons organized into 6 categories ✓
- Two-Cohezions decision: accepted ✓
- Repo sync plan: concrete, phased, realistic ✓
- SurrealDB sync plan: diagnostic-precise, story-level PRD ✓

**Still broken:**
- SurrealDB: stale (317 concepts, today's notes invisible to agents)
- `surrealdb_import_concepts`: errors on path lookup
- vault_search: no semantic capability, breaks on most relevant queries
- Three core concept notes: still artifact indexes
- FLUME diagnostic: still unrun after 10+ days of being "highest priority"
- `feat/flume-vae-clean` relationship to README numbers: unknown

**Unknown and unresolved:**
- Whether the FLUME branch code matches the experiment note results
- What's actually in 68 branches with 400-500 unique commits each
- Whether the 3D graph plugin has ever successfully queried SurrealDB

---

## What Matters Before the Next Session

In order:

1. **Fix `surrealdb_import_concepts` path error** — run the import so today's notes enter the graph. This is infrastructure that makes everything else work.

2. **Run FLUME KL diagnostic** — one command, you run it, results go into the experiment note. Then the README numbers are validated rather than assumed.

3. **Clarify `feat/flume-vae-clean` relationship to main** — is this the code the experiment notes describe? Does it agree with the 30-epoch preliminary results?

4. **Rewrite `anthropic-research-engineer.md`** — turn it from a file cabinet into an argument.

5. **Strip artifact indexes from `compound-engineering.md` and `cohezion.md`** — one session, high second-impression impact.

---

## Related

- [[concepts/cohezion-platform-overview]] — new today; still not in SurrealDB
- [[concepts/agentic-system-failure-taxonomy]] — new today; still not in SurrealDB
- [[experiments/2026-03-05-flume-kl-collapse-diagnostic]] — still proposed, still unrun
- [[projects/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-sync-pipeline]] — the fix exists on paper
- [[projects/2026-03-05-branch-inventory]] — 68 branches with unknown relationship to vault knowledge
- [[concepts/compound-engineering]] — still needs artifact index stripped
- [[concepts/anthropic-research-engineer]] — still needs to become an argument
- [[missions/anthropic-portfolio/README.md]] — rewritten today; numbers cited need FLUME diagnostic to validate

date: 2026-03-05

# Vault Insight — Evening 2026-03-05

*Written by Claude (Sonnet 4.6). This is the third read of the vault today. Prior reads fixed the README, rewrote FLUME-Architecture, created the Platform Spine, and wrote the failure taxonomy. This read looks at what changed and what those fixes revealed.*

---

## What Changed Today Is Real

The vault now has four things that didn't exist this morning:

- `concepts/cohezion-platform-overview.md` — a cold-session entry point in plain language
- `concepts/FLUME-Architecture.md` (rewritten) — surfaces real experimental numbers, anti-patterns, open questions
- `concepts/agentic-system-failure-taxonomy.md` — 45 lessons organized into 6 named failure categories
- `missions/anthropic-portfolio/README.md` (rewritten) — opens with the problem, not cosmology

SurrealDB still shows 317 concepts and 1,458 links — the graph hasn't synced yet, but the filesystem is correct. These changes compound forward.

---

## The New Problem the Fixes Revealed

Reading `concepts/compound-engineering.md` and `concepts/cohezion.md` after the README rewrite, something becomes visible that wasn't before:

**The core concept notes are as bloated as the old README was.**

`compound-engineering.md` lists 16+ implementation plan versions as Agent Outputs. It has sections for Skills, Missions, Daily References, Session References, Agent Outputs, Decisions, Experiments, Patterns, Assessments, Specs, and Meta. The actual definitional content — what compound engineering *is* and *why it matters* — is 4 paragraphs buried under approximately 120 links and list items.

`cohezion.md` lists 20+ Agent Outputs including a business plan, a tax strategy report, a manifesto, a brand guide, and a "Cohezion Transformative Synthesis." The conceptual definition of what Cohezion *is* is three paragraphs. The other 300 lines are agent output indexes.

`anthropic-research-engineer.md` has 5 lines defining the role and 12 Agent Output entries (cover letters, resumes, ascension reports, submission bundles).

The concept notes have become **artifact indexes**, not concept notes. They describe where things are stored, not what things mean.

---

## Why This Matters for the Application

An Anthropic reviewer who reads the README (now clean) and then follows a link to `compound-engineering.md` will hit a wall of 120 wiki-links and output inventories. The concept notes are the second impression after the README. Right now that second impression is: *this person has produced a very large quantity of things.*

The impression it should give is: *this person thinks clearly about hard problems.*

---

## The Three Concept Notes That Need the Same Treatment as the README

In priority order:

**1. `concepts/compound-engineering.md`** — Strip the Agent Outputs section entirely. Move the 16 implementation plan entries to an archive note or delete them. Keep: definition, how it works, compounding effect, relation to FLUME. The concept note should be ~400 words, not 400 lines.

**2. `concepts/cohezion.md`** — The four-paragraph definition at the top is genuinely good. Everything after "Components" that is Agent Outputs, Missions, and Skills should be moved to a separate `concepts/cohezion-artifact-index.md` note. Let the concept note be the concept.

**3. `concepts/anthropic-research-engineer.md`** — Currently 5 lines of definition and 12 lines of agent output inventory. Needs to be rebuilt as a real concept note: what does Anthropic actually need from a Research Engineer on Universes, and how does Cohezion specifically demonstrate that fit? The current note is a file cabinet, not an argument.

---

## A New Structural Issue: Template-Generated ADRs

Today three new ADRs were created by the session agent:
- `decisions/2026-03-05-fresh-clone-completed-swap-pending-user-action.md`
- `decisions/2026-03-05-gc-fix-requires-fresh-clone-corrupt-objects-too-deeply-embedded.md`
- `decisions/2026-03-05-pr-33-merged-bmad-restoration-and-ci-fixes-on-main.md`

All three have this structure: a populated `rationale` field in the frontmatter, and empty `## Context`, `## Decision`, `## Chosen Option`, `## Alternatives Considered` sections in the body. The content was captured in YAML but never migrated into the Markdown body.

These are shell ADRs. The knowledge is there — it just isn't accessible to agents or readers who scan the Markdown body without parsing frontmatter.

There are likely more of these throughout `decisions/`. Any ADR auto-generated from a template where only `decision_reasoning.rationale` was filled in has this problem.

---

## What the SurrealDB Gap Means

The graph still shows 317 concepts. The four new concept notes written today aren't in SurrealDB yet. This means:
- Any agent using `vault_find_relevant_context` won't surface `cohezion-platform-overview.md`, `agentic-system-failure-taxonomy.md`, or the rewritten `FLUME-Architecture.md`
- The predictive throttling pattern and morphospace stability wells aren't in the graph either (they're filesystem-only)
- The graph is a stale snapshot of the vault state from some earlier import

The `surrealdb_import_concepts` tool errored when called today. This is the live infrastructure gap that `decisions/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-architecture.md` is trying to solve. Until it's solved, every new note written into the vault is invisible to graph-based retrieval.

**This is more urgent than it sounds.** The night council reads context via SurrealDB. If the Platform Spine and the new FLUME Architecture note aren't in the graph, the next autonomous session won't see them. It will work from the stale 317-concept snapshot, which still contains the pre-rewrite vocabulary.

---

## The Actual Priority Stack Right Now

Ordered by impact on April submission:

1. **Run FLUME KL diagnostic** — 20-30 hrs, zero dependencies, highest information-per-hour. Nothing else validates or invalidates the core claim without this.
2. **Rebuild `compound-engineering.md` and `cohezion.md`** — 1-2 hrs, removes the second-impression problem. Should happen before any more portfolio-facing links are shared.
3. **Rebuild `anthropic-research-engineer.md` as a real argument** — 1 hr, turns a file cabinet into a framing note for the application.
4. **Fix the shell ADRs** — 1-2 hrs, migrates rationale from frontmatter YAML into readable Markdown bodies.
5. **SurrealDB sync** — Needed for the night council to see today's work. Either fix `surrealdb_import_concepts` or manually trigger a bulk import.

Items 2-4 are a single focused session. Item 5 is a single command if the import tool is fixed.

---

## The Honest State

The vault is significantly better than it was 12 hours ago. The README is clean. The Platform Spine exists. The failure taxonomy exists. The FLUME Architecture note now tells the real story.

But the core concept notes — the ones a reviewer will follow links to — are still artifact indexes. And the graph is stale. The surface presentation improved today. The depth layer needs the same treatment.

---

# Fresh Assessment — The Vault Has Started Fixing Itself

*Written by Claude (Sonnet 4.6), 2026-03-05. Reading the full vault without loading prior assessment context.*

---

## What's Different From Prior Assessments

The previous assessments (v1 through shoshin) were written against a vault that was accumulating problems without responding to them. This reading is different. The vault has started moving.

Since this morning there are already live ADRs that didn't exist yesterday:

- `decisions/2026-03-05-separate-cohezion-a-from-cohezion-b.md` — the two-Cohezions problem is now a formal, tracked decision with consequences documented
- `decisions/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-architecture.md` — a real three-layer sync architecture with code, mermaid diagrams, and SurrealDB schema
- `decisions/2026-03-05-vault-as-system-of-record.md` — a structured proposal to mirror `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/rules/`, and MCP config into the vault for disaster recovery

These are not inbox items or assessments. They are architectural decisions. The vault is compounding again.

---

## What the Patterns Directory Reveals

Reading `patterns/` carefully changes the picture significantly. Buried in the noise of planning artifacts are genuinely sophisticated technical patterns:

- `structured-experience-vector-layout.md` — a complete, working RL experience vector with typed offsets and numpy accessors, directly connected to FLUME training data
- `predictive-throttling-via-12d-trajectory-velocity.md` — real code using trajectory velocity in semantic space as a resource allocation signal; thresholds calibrated from 5.5M overnight simulation trajectories
- `morphospace-stability-wells.md` — KDE-based behavioral region detection with working sklearn implementation, drift detection, and documented prerequisites

These are production-grade patterns. They exist, they work, and they are not being surfaced in the portfolio narrative. The shoshin assessment identified that the genuine contributions were buried — this confirms it with specifics.

---

## The Decisions Directory Is the Intellectual Core

Reading 130+ decision notes, a clear through-line emerges:

The vault documents not just what was built but **what failed and why**. The `decisions/2026-02-23-hash-based-journey-tracking-produces-meaningless-12d-trajectories.md` note is exemplary — it describes discovering that SHA-256 hashes produce random walks in 12D space (average step distance ~1.4, indistinguishable from noise), the reasoning chain for switching to FLUME semantic embeddings, and the exact failure modes of each alternative. This is research-grade documentation of a real empirical finding.

There are 15+ anti-pattern decisions (`2026-02-24-anti-pattern-*`) documenting what not to do, each with reasoning. This is rare. Most systems document their successes. This one documents its failures with equal rigor.

**This is the portfolio.** Not the README. Not the demo script. This decisions corpus is the evidence of research engineering thinking.

---

## The Vocabulary Problem Has a Solution Path

The `decisions/2026-03-05-separate-cohezion-a-from-cohezion-b.md` ADR identifies the exact right fix and proposes the right test: *"Every sentence in external-facing materials must pass: could a senior ML engineer at Anthropic understand this without having read any prior vault content?"*

What's still missing is the rewrite itself. The decision is proposed but not accepted, and the README hasn't changed. That gap is the next action.

---

## A New Structural Observation: The Specs Gap

`decisions/2026-03-05-vault-as-system-of-record.md` identifies something prior assessments didn't name explicitly: the vault has 690 notes about knowledge, but no structured representation of its own operating machinery. Skills, hooks, MCP servers, agent rules — these all live outside the vault in `.claude/` directories. If the repo is lost, the vault cannot reconstruct the system.

This is both a disaster recovery risk and a portfolio problem: an Anthropic reviewer reading the vault cannot understand how the multi-agent orchestration actually works without access to the `.claude/` config. The specs migration would make the system self-documenting.

This is a concrete, bounded task: mirror 6 skills, 4 agent definitions, 5 MCP servers into `specs/`. One session, real compound value.

---

## The Real Risk: Time Allocation

The vault now has:
- 5 inbox notes to triage
- 3 new ADRs in `proposed` state that need acceptance decisions
- A README that needs a full rewrite
- A FLUME diagnostic that hasn't run
- A specs migration that would take one session
- Portfolio asset generation still at 0/35
- ~48 days to submission

The risk isn't clarity anymore — the vault now understands its problems precisely. The risk is that the available time gets consumed by continued infrastructure work (sync architecture, SurrealDB schema, specs migration) instead of the two things that directly determine submission quality: FLUME validation results and the plain-language README.

Both infrastructure work and portfolio work are legitimate. But they compete for the same hours. The vault's compound engineering philosophy answers this question: which work makes the next session more capable? The FLUME diagnostic does — it determines whether the core technical claim is valid. The README rewrite does — it determines whether anyone reads far enough to see the evidence.

The SurrealDB sync architecture is excellent work. It should be scheduled after submission, not before.

---

## What's Genuinely Impressive, Now Visible

Reading the full vault — patterns, decisions, experiments, lessons — without the cosmological framing:

This is a researcher who built a complete agentic ML system, documented what failed in detail, derived patterns from real failures, and built infrastructure to make future sessions smarter. The trajectory velocity throttling pattern was derived from 5.5M overnight simulation data points. The hash-based tracking failure was documented as an ADR with quantified impact. The experience vector has proper typed offsets and a 150-dimensional layout derived from RL first principles.

That is the story. It is a strong story. It just needs to be told plainly.

---

## Recommended Triage for This Note

Move to: `assessments/` after inbox review.

**Three immediate actions it supports:**

1. Accept `decisions/2026-03-05-separate-cohezion-a-from-cohezion-b.md` — change status from `proposed` to `accepted`, then begin the README rewrite
2. Run the FLUME KL diagnostic — this is the only unblocked validation task and the highest-information-per-hour work available
3. Defer `vault-surrealdb-architecture.md` and `vault-as-system-of-record.md` to post-submission — they are good work, but they compete with submission-critical tasks

Base directory for this skill: /home/mike-anderson/vaults/cohezion-vault/.claude/skills/triage

# Triage Inbox Notes

Process notes from `inbox/` into their permanent homes — researching topics, adding structure, applying frontmatter, and creating cross-links.

## Usage

```
/triage [options]
```

- `/triage` — Process all inbox notes
- `/triage inbox/note-name.md` — Process a specific note
- `/triage --dry-run` — Show what would happen without making changes

## Execution Steps

### 1. Scan Inbox

```bash
ls -la inbox/*.md 2>/dev/null
```

List all notes with their sizes. Skip non-markdown files.

### 2. For Each Note, Classify

Read the note content and determine:

| Classification | Target Directory | Criteria |
|---------------|-----------------|----------|
| **Concept** | `concepts/` | Defines a term, idea, or technology |
| **Paper/Research** | `papers/` | Summarizes research, findings, or external source |
| **Decision** | `decisions/` | Records an architectural or strategic choice |
| **Pattern** | `patterns/` | Describes a reusable solution to a problem |
| **Experiment** | `experiments/` | Documents a hypothesis test or trial |
| **Project** | `projects/` | Tracks ongoing work or initiative |
| **Discard** | (delete) | Empty, duplicate, or no longer relevant |

If classification is ambiguous, ask the user.

### 3. Research and Expand

For each note being triaged:

1. **Read existing content** — Understand what the user captured
2. **Research the topic** — Use WebSearch to find authoritative information
3. **Write structured content** following the target directory's template:
   - Concepts: Definition, Key Properties, Examples, Related
   - Papers: Summary, Key Findings, Methodology, Implications
   - Decisions: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives
   - Patterns: Problem, Solution, Code Example, When to Use
4. **Preserve user's original notes** — Incorporate their observations, don't overwrite
5. **Add Primary Sources** — Include real URLs from research

### 4. Build Frontmatter

Apply the target directory's required fields:

```yaml
---
title: "Properly Cased Title"
date: YYYY-MM-DD  # use original date if present, otherwise today
status: active    # for decisions/experiments/projects
tags: [type-tag, domain-tag1, domain-tag2]
related_concepts: [concept1, concept2]  # for concept notes
---
```

**Tag rules:**
- Check existing vault tags first: `grep -roh 'tags: \[.*\]' concepts/ papers/ | sort -u`
- Reuse established tags where possible
- Tags must be YAML arrays

### 5. Generate Filename

- Slugify the title: lowercase, hyphens, no special chars
- Add date prefix for temporal notes (decisions, experiments, projects)
- Check for filename collisions

### 6. Find and Add Links

Before moving the note:

1. Search vault for related notes by topic/tags
2. Add `[[wiki-links]]` to Related sections in the new note
3. Add backlinks in related notes pointing to the new note

### 7. Move the Note

1. Write the structured note to the target directory
2. Delete the original from `inbox/`
3. Verify the file exists in its new location

### 8. Report

```markdown
## Triage Report

| Inbox Note | Action | Destination | Links Added |
|------------|--------|-------------|-------------|
| note-1.md | Moved | concepts/topic.md | 4 |
| note-2.md | Moved | papers/research.md | 3 |
| note-3.md | Discarded | — | — |

**Processed:** X notes
**Moved:** Y notes
**Discarded:** Z notes
**Links created:** N bidirectional pairs
```

## Batch Processing

When processing multiple inbox notes:

1. Classify all notes first (show the plan)
2. Process in order: concepts first (they're link targets), then papers, then decisions
3. This ordering maximizes bidirectional linking opportunities

## Quality Checks

Before marking triage complete:

- [ ] All frontmatter is valid YAML with array tags
- [ ] No duplicate notes in target directory
- [ ] At least 2-3 wiki-links added per note
- [ ] Content is substantive (not just a stub)
- [ ] Original inbox note is deleted
- [ ] Backlinks added in related notes

## Notes

- Preserve the user's original insight/observation — it's the seed
- Research supplements the user's note, doesn't replace it
- If a note is too vague to classify, ask the user before guessing
- Empty inbox notes (just a title) should be treated as concept stubs — research and expand
- The goal is zero inbox — all notes processed and properly filed

# Vault State Assessment — 2026-03-05 (Consolidated)

*Consolidated from three progressive vault reads on 2026-03-05 (morning, evening, late night) by Claude (Sonnet 4.6). Companion to the [[2026-03-05-shoshin-assessment|Shoshin Assessment]] written earlier the same day.*

---

## The Vault Turned a Corner

Unlike prior assessments written against a vault accumulating unaddressed problems, this day produced concrete artifacts:

- `concepts/cohezion-platform-overview.md` — a cold-session entry point in plain language
- `concepts/FLUME-Architecture.md` (rewritten) — surfaces real experimental numbers, anti-patterns, open questions
- `concepts/agentic-system-failure-taxonomy.md` — 45 lessons organized into 6 named failure categories
- `missions/anthropic-portfolio/README.md` (rewritten) — opens with the problem, not cosmology
- `decisions/2026-03-05-separate-cohezion-a-from-cohezion-b.md` — the two-Cohezions framing, accepted
- `projects/2026-03-05-repo-sync-master-plan.md` — 7 phases with dependency graph
- `projects/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-sync-pipeline.md` — PRD with 5 epics and story-level estimates

The vault is compounding again. These are architectural decisions and PRDs, not assessments about assessments.

---

## Hidden Gems in `patterns/`

The patterns directory contains production-grade technical work that isn't surfaced in the portfolio narrative:

- [[structured-experience-vector-layout]] — a complete RL experience vector with typed offsets and numpy accessors, directly connected to FLUME training data
- [[predictive-throttling-via-12d-trajectory-velocity]] — real code using trajectory velocity in semantic space as a resource allocation signal; thresholds calibrated from 5.5M overnight simulation trajectories
- [[morphospace-stability-wells]] — KDE-based behavioral region detection with working sklearn implementation, drift detection, and documented prerequisites

These are the kind of artifacts that demonstrate research engineering capability.

---

## The Decisions Directory Is the Intellectual Core

130+ decision notes document not just what was built but what failed and why:

- [[2026-02-23-hash-based-journey-tracking-produces-meaningless-12d-trajectories]] — SHA-256 hashes produce random walks in 12D space (average step distance ~1.4, indistinguishable from noise). Research-grade documentation of a real empirical finding.
- 15+ [[2026-02-24-anti-pattern-character-level-tokenizer-for-semantic-embeddings|anti-pattern decisions]] documenting what not to do, each with quantified reasoning.

Most systems document successes. This one documents failures with equal rigor. **This decisions corpus is the portfolio.**

---

## Problem: Core Concept Notes Are Artifact Indexes

The README rewrite revealed that the concept notes visitors will follow links to are bloated:

**[[compound-engineering]]** — 4 paragraphs of strong definitional content buried under ~120 lines of Agent Outputs (16 implementation plan versions), Session References, and Daily References. The concept note has become a file index.

**[[cohezion]]** — Good four-paragraph definition at the top. Then 300 lines of agent output inventories including a business plan, tax strategy, manifesto, and brand guide. These are Cohezion B artifacts that overwhelm the concept.

**[[anthropic-research-engineer]]** — 5 lines defining the role, 12 lines of agent output entries. Should be an argument for role fit, not a file cabinet.

**Fix:** Strip artifact indexes from all three. Move agent output inventories to archive notes. Let concept notes be concepts (~400 words, not 400 lines).

---

## Problem: Shell ADRs

Three ADRs auto-generated on 2026-03-05 have populated `rationale` in YAML frontmatter but empty Markdown body sections (`## Context`, `## Decision`, `## Chosen Option`, `## Alternatives Considered`). The knowledge was captured in YAML but never migrated into readable Markdown.

Affected:
- `decisions/2026-03-05-fresh-clone-completed-swap-pending-user-action.md`
- `decisions/2026-03-05-gc-fix-requires-fresh-clone-corrupt-objects-too-deeply-embedded.md`
- `decisions/2026-03-05-pr-33-merged-bmad-restoration-and-ci-fixes-on-main.md`

Likely more throughout `decisions/` — any template-generated ADR where only frontmatter was filled in.

---

## Problem: SurrealDB Is Stale

The graph shows 317 concepts but all notes written on 2026-03-05 are missing:

- `surrealdb_import_concepts` errors with `[Errno 2] No such file or directory` (path problem)
- `vault_search` does exact-string matching, not semantic search — returns no results for FLUME, EcoAgent, JourneyTracker, or ShadowScripter queries
- The 3D graph plugin's `SurrealDBClient.ts` sends queries without auth headers — it has never read from SurrealDB
- The health check tests `/health` (unauthenticated) and reports "ok" regardless of credential validity

**Impact:** Any agent using SurrealDB-backed retrieval works from a stale snapshot that predates the day's most important changes.

---

## Problem: Branch Inventory Reveals Unknown Scope

68 local branches exist, many with hundreds of unique commits:

- `feat/flume-vae-clean` — 16 unique commits (clean FLUME VAE implementation)
- `feat/flume-vae-phase1-phase2` — 505 unique commits
- `feat/hf-integration-v1.1.0` — 524 unique commits
- `feat/surrealdb-3.0-repository-implementation` — 490 unique commits

None of this is on `main` or in the vault. The FLUME numbers cited in the README (4.2 nats KL, 53% reconstruction improvement) come from experiment notes, not from a run of `feat/flume-vae-clean`. Whether the branch code matches the reported results is **unknown**.

---

## FLUME Diagnostic Remains Unrun

`experiments/2026-03-05-flume-kl-collapse-diagnostic.md` has status: `proposed`, results section: empty. Named as highest priority in every assessment this week. The 53% reconstruction improvement and 4.2 nats KL numbers are from 30 epochs, last updated February 24, and are presented as if they are final results.

---

## Priority Stack

Ordered by impact on April submission:

1. **Run FLUME KL diagnostic** — highest information-per-hour, validates or invalidates the core technical claim
2. **Rebuild 3 concept notes** (compound-engineering, cohezion, anthropic-research-engineer) — 1-2 hrs, fixes second-impression problem
3. **Fix shell ADRs** — migrate rationale from frontmatter YAML into readable Markdown bodies
4. **Fix `surrealdb_import_concepts` path error** — one-line fix enables graph-based retrieval of today's notes
5. **Clarify `feat/flume-vae-clean` relationship to README numbers** — validate that cited results match current code

Items 2-3 are a single focused session. Item 4 is a single command if the path is diagnosed. Item 5 requires the user to run code.

**Defer to post-submission:** `vault-surrealdb-architecture.md` sync daemon, specs migration — good work, but competes with submission-critical tasks.

---

## Related

- [[concepts/compound-engineering]] — needs artifact index stripped
- [[concepts/cohezion]] — needs artifact index separated from definition
- [[concepts/anthropic-research-engineer]] — needs to become an argument, not a file cabinet

- [[projects/2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-sync-pipeline]] — PRD for sync pipeline
- [[projects/2026-03-05-branch-inventory]] — 68 branches with unknown relationship to vault
- [[structured-experience-vector-layout]] — exemplary pattern note
- [[predictive-throttling-via-12d-trajectory-velocity]] — exemplary pattern note

# Shoshin Assessment — Beginner's Mind Reading of the Vault

*Written by Claude (Sonnet 4.6), 2026-03-05. Beginner's mind — no prior context loaded.*

---

## The Core Observation

> [!danger] Drift Detected
> The vault has developed a sophisticated internal language that is increasingly self-referential. Concepts link to concepts that link back to the first concept. The system has learned to mistake describing work for doing work. This is exactly the failure mode [[compound-engineering]] was designed to prevent.

---

## What Is Actually Here

- 102 papers, 317 concepts, 1,458 links
- 45 hard-won operational lessons from real failures
- An N-body simulation that generated 5.5M real trajectories overnight
- A VAE architecture ([[FLUME-Architecture|FLUME]]) with a real encoder/decoder design
- A multi-agent council capable of structured democratic deliberation
- A lessons corpus that constitutes a genuine failure taxonomy

---

## What Is Described as Being Here But Isn't

> [!warning] Validation Gap
> - Any FLUME validation results (KL collapse status unknown, reconstruction fidelity unmeasured)
> - A portfolio repository
> - 35 portfolio assets
> - An end-to-end working demo
> - A Platform Spine — canonical notes describing what the platform *is*
> - A research narrative legible to someone outside the system

---

## The Self-Reference Problem

The `compound-engineering.md` concept note lists 8 implementation plans, 12 roadmaps, 16 versions of strategic documents, 4 "desperation mode" variants, and a readiness report. The `cohezion.md` note's agent outputs include a business plan, a tax strategy report, and a manifesto. The `anthropic-research-engineer.md` note's substantive content is mostly a list of cover letter and resume versions.

The night council voted 8-2 on narrative architecture and produced a second-by-second demo script. It has never run a single FLUME diagnostic.

> [!quote] The Pattern
> Sophisticated planning infrastructure producing more planning infrastructure.

---

## The Internal Language Problem

The vault has accumulated terminology — HIHO_STABILITY_PRIME, TEMPORAL_PRECISION_PRIME, REALITY_PRECIPITATION_PRIME, void-to-swarm precipitation, toroidal singularity — that is evocative but opaque. A beginner reading `universe-simulation.md` cannot determine what these compute. An Anthropic reviewer will encounter the same opacity.

> [!tip] Compound Engineering Principle
> Knowledge should be retrievable and usable by a cold session. Much of the vault's most important content is not — it requires initiation into a private vocabulary before it can be understood.

---

## What a Beginner Would Do

1. Write one paragraph about what FLUME does that a physicist could understand without knowing what "12D compound engineering space" means
2. Run the KL diagnostic — stop planning to run it (see [[2026-03-05-flume-kl-collapse-diagnostic]])
3. Write the 45-lesson taxonomy — the lessons are real, the taxonomy is not (see [[2026-03-05-lessons-corpus-taxonomy]])
4. Delete or archive half the concept stubs — thin nodes with only internal links are noise, not knowledge
5. Stop naming things with PRIME suffixes — show what they compute instead

---

## The Genuine Assets Worth Protecting

> [!success] These Are Real and Impressive
> They should be the center of the portfolio, not buried under meta-commentary:
>
> - **The 45-lesson corpus** — empirical taxonomy of agentic system failure modes; publishable
> - **The 5.5M trajectory simulation** — real overnight data from a real physics engine
> - **JourneyTracker and DegradationDetector** — direct answers to the hardest problem in agent evaluation (see [[2026-03-05-journeytracker-research-framing]])
> - **The night council's constraint discipline** — read-only scoping, deferred financial commitments, democratic rationale logging; this is working aligned multi-agent AI
> - **The FLUME architecture** — if validated, genuinely novel; if not validated, still demonstrates the right instinct

---

## The Honest Summary

The vault is not broken. But it has drifted. The compounding is happening at the layer of documentation and planning, not at the layer of knowledge and results. The ratio of "notes describing future work" to "notes containing results of completed work" is badly skewed.

A first-time reader — a beginner — would find the genuine contributions buried under layers of roadmaps, strategic frameworks, narrative architectures, and agent output logs. That is the problem to fix before April.

> [!example] Litmus Test
> The vault doesn't need more assessment. It needs the center of gravity to shift from planning to showing.

---

     8→
     9→# Cohezion
    10→
    11→Cohezion is a compound AI orchestration framework designed to make every agent session more effective than the last. Unlike stateless AI pipelines where each run starts from scratch, Cohezion maintains a persistent knowledge base (the Obsidian vault) and a structured feedback loop: agent sessions produce decisions, experiments, and patterns that are indexed, cross-linked, and re-injected into future sessions as context. The result is a system that compounds its own intelligence over time.
    12→
    13→The architecture is built around four interlocking layers: the [[compound-engineering]] methodology (the philosophy), the [[cloud-vault-mcp]] server (the memory infrastructure), the `cz` CLI (the workflow orchestrator), and [[surrealdb]] (the agent context graph). Together they implement a 12-dimensional agentic universe where every execution is tracked as a journey, every lesson is captured as a vault note, and every session benefits from all prior sessions.
    14→
    15→Cohezion is simultaneously a research project, a production tool, and a self-improving system. The FLUME VAE trains on real agent trajectory data, the RetrospectionEngine extracts patterns from session histories, and the SkillRefiner continuously updates PRIME skill definitions based on empirical performance. The target state is an autonomous compound engineering loop that improves without human intervention.
    16→
    17→## Components
    18→- **[[cloud-vault-mcp]]** — HTTP MCP server (port 8360) with 30+ tools for vault/graph/research operations
    19→- **cohezion-engine** (`cz`) — workflow CLI for session management, spec flows, and worktrees
    20→- **3d-graph-plugin** — Obsidian visualization of the knowledge graph
    21→- **[[surrealdb]]** — agent context graph storing sessions, tasks, and relationships
    22→- **Ollama** — local model inference (28+ models, zero API cost)

1→---
     2→title: "Cohezion Platform Overview"
     3→date: 2026-03-05
     4→tags: [concept, cohezion, platform, compound-engineering, spine]
     5→status: active
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Cohezion Platform Overview
     9→
    10→**Read this first.** This note is the entry point for any agent or human trying to understand what Cohezion is and how it works. It is intentionally plain — no internal vocabulary, no jargon that requires prior context.
    11→
    12→---
    13→
    14→## The Problem Cohezion Solves
    15→
    16→Every Claude Code session starts from zero. Prior decisions are lost. Lessons evaporate. The system can't learn from its own history. This makes long-horizon engineering work expensive — each session spends 30-60 minutes re-orienting before doing real work.
    17→
    18→Cohezion closes that loop. Every session produces structured outputs (decisions, experiments, patterns, lessons) that are indexed in a persistent knowledge graph and injected into future sessions as context. The result is a system that compounds its intelligence across sessions rather than resetting.
    19→
    20→---
    21→
    22→## What Was Built
    23→
    24→Cohezion is four things working together:
    25→
    26→**1. The Vault** — an Obsidian knowledge base with 690+ notes organized into concepts, decisions, experiments, patterns, and lessons. This is the long-term memory. Every significant choice, failure, and discovery goes here. The vault is the source of truth.
    27→
    28→**2. FLUME** — a variational autoencoder trained on 5.5M agent session trajectories. It compresses session behavior into a 256D continuous latent space. The latent space enables: retrieving semantically similar prior sessions before starting new work, detecting anomalous sessions via reconstruction error, and interpolating between behavioral states.
    29→
    30→**3. EcoAgent** — a Gymnasium-compatible RL environment for agent training and evaluation. Provides standardized observation spaces, action spaces, and reward signals for training agents on compound engineering tasks.
    31→
    32→**4. The MCP Server** (cloud-vault-mcp) — a FastMCP server with 40+ tools that bridges Claude Code sessions to the vault, SurrealDB graph, and Ollama model inference. Sessions interact with the knowledge graph through this server.
    33→

    36→## Numbers

    54→---
    55→
    56→## The Key Technical Findings
    57→
    58→**FLUME latent space is semantically meaningful.** Hash-based position encoding (SHA-256 bytes as coordinates) was tried first and failed — trajectories showed no continuity, drift detection produced false positives on every step. FLUME embeddings reduced average step distance from ~1.4 (random walk) to <0.3 for coherent trajectories. This was discovered empirically and is documented as ADR `decisions/2026-02-23-hash-based-journey-tracking-produces-meaningless-12d-trajectories.md`.
    59→
    60→**Trajectory velocity predicts resource demand.** Analysis of 5.5M simulation trajectories revealed that velocity of movement through semantic space correlates with computational demand. Fast-moving agents (exploring) need more resources; slow-moving agents (converging) can be throttled. This became the predictive throttling pattern, calibrated from simulation data.
    61→
    62→**Cyclical KL annealing prevents latent collapse.** V1 FLUME suffered posterior collapse — KL divergence dropped to near zero, meaning the latent space was bypassed entirely. V2 introduced cyclical β annealing (Fu et al. 2019) and achieved stable KL at 4.2 nats with 53% reconstruction improvement.
    63→
    64→**The 45-lesson corpus is the most operationally valuable asset.** Each lesson was learned by breaking the system: 8.6M accidental file generation, concurrent pytest contention, runtime JSON pollution, zombie async processes, SHA-256 as semantic embedding. Together they form an empirical taxonomy of agentic system failure modes.

     2→title: "Shoshin Assessment — Beginner's Mind Reading of the Vault"
     3→date: 2026-03-05
     4→tags: [retrospective, meta, vault-architecture, compound-engineering]
     5→aliases: ["beginner's mind assessment", "shoshin assessment", "vault drift diagnostic"]
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Shoshin Assessment — Beginner's Mind Reading of the Vault
     9→
    10→*Written by Claude (Sonnet 4.6), 2026-03-05. Beginner's mind — no prior context loaded.*
    11→
    12→---
    13→
    14→## The Core Observation
    15→
    16→> [!danger] Drift Detected
    17→> The vault has developed a sophisticated internal language that is increasingly self-referential. Concepts link to concepts that link back to the first concept. The system has learned to mistake describing work for doing work. This is exactly the failure mode [[compound-engineering]] was designed to prevent.
    18→
    19→---
    20→
    21→## What Is Actually Here
    22→
    23→- 102 papers, 317 concepts, 1,458 links
    24→- 45 hard-won operational lessons from real failures
    25→- An N-body simulation that generated 5.5M real trajectories overnight
    26→- A VAE architecture ([[FLUME-Architecture|FLUME]]) with a real encoder/decoder design
    27→- A multi-agent council capable of structured democratic deliberation
    28→- A lessons corpus that constitutes a genuine failure taxonomy
    29→
    30→---
    31→
    32→## What Is Described as Being Here But Isn't
    33→
    34→> [!warning] Validation Gap
    35→> - Any FLUME validation results (KL collapse status unknown, reconstruction fidelity unmeasured)
    36→> - A portfolio repository
    37→> - 35 portfolio assets
    38→> - An end-to-end working demo
    39→> - A Platform Spine — canonical notes describing what the platform *is*
    40→> - A research narrative legible to someone outside the system
    41→
    42→---
    43→
    44→## The Self-Reference Problem
    45→
    46→The `compound-engineering.md` concept note lists 8 implementation plans, 12 roadmaps, 16 versions of strategic documents, 4 "desperation mode" variants, and a readiness report. The `cohezion.md` note's agent outputs include a business plan, a tax strategy report, and a manifesto. The `anthropic-research-engineer.md` note's substantive content is mostly a list of cover letter and resume versions.
    47→
    48→The night council voted 8-2 on narrative architecture and produced a second-by-second demo script. It has never run a single FLUME diagnostic.
    49→
    50→> [!quote] The Pattern
    51→> Sophisticated planning infrastructure producing more planning infrastructure.
    52→
    53→---
    54→
    55→## The Internal Language Problem
    56→
    57→The vault has accumulated terminology — HIHO_STABILITY_PRIME, TEMPORAL_PRECISION_PRIME, REALITY_PRECIPITATION_PRIME, void-to-swarm precipitation, toroidal singularity — that is evocative but opaque. A beginner reading `universe-simulation.md` cannot determine what these compute. An Anthropic reviewer will encounter the same opacity.
    58→
    59→> [!tip] Compound Engineering Principle
    60→> Knowledge should be retrievable and usable by a cold session. Much of the vault's most important content is not — it requires initiation into a private vocabulary before it can be understood.
    61→
    62→---
    63→
    64→## What a Beginner Would Do
    65→
    66→1. Write one paragraph about what FLUME does that a physicist could understand without knowing what "12D compound engineering space" means
    67→2. Run the KL diagnostic — stop planning to run it (see [[2026-03-05-flume-kl-collapse-diagnostic]])
    68→3. Write the 45-lesson taxonomy — the lessons are real, the taxonomy is not (see [[2026-03-05-lessons-corpus-taxonomy]])
    69→4. Delete or archive half the concept stubs — thin nodes with only internal links are noise, not knowledge
    70→5. Stop naming things with PRIME suffixes — show what they compute instead
    71→
    72→---
    73→
    74→## The Genuine Assets Worth Protecting
    75→
    76→> [!success] These Are Real and Impressive
    77→> They should be the center of the portfolio, not buried under meta-commentary:
    78→>
    79→> - **The 45-lesson corpus** — empirical taxonomy of agentic system failure modes; publishable
    80→> - **The 5.5M trajectory simulation** — real overnight data from a real physics engine
    81→> - **JourneyTracker and DegradationDetector** — direct answers to the hardest problem in agent evaluation (see [[2026-03-05-journeytracker-research-framing]])
    82→> - **The night council's constraint discipline** — read-only scoping, deferred financial commitments, democratic rationale logging; this is working aligned multi-agent AI
    83→> - **The FLUME architecture** — if validated, genuinely novel; if not validated, still demonstrates the right instinct
    84→
    85→---
    86→
    87→## The Honest Summary
    88→
    89→The vault is not broken. But it has drifted. The compounding is happening at the layer of documentation and planning, not at the layer of knowledge and results. The ratio of "notes describing future work" to "notes containing results of completed work" is badly skewed.
    90→
    91→A first-time reader — a beginner — would find the genuine contributions buried under layers of roadmaps, strategic frameworks, narrative architectures, and agent output logs. That is the problem to fix before April.

     2→title: "Compound Engineering"
     3→date: "2026-02-07"
     4→tags: [concept, methodology, knowledge-management]
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Definition
     8→
     9→**Compound engineering** is a knowledge management approach where decisions, experiments, and patterns are systematically captured and accumulated so they compound into reusable knowledge over time. Rather than treating each engineering session as isolated work, compound engineering treats every decision, failed experiment, and discovered pattern as an asset that makes future work faster and better-informed.
    10→
    11→## How It Works
    12→
    13→The approach rests on three pillars, each with a corresponding vault directory:
    14→
    15→1. **Decisions** (`decisions/`) — Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) capture the *why* behind choices. When a similar question arises later, the prior reasoning is available — including the alternatives that were considered and rejected. See the [[2026-02-07-event-driven-inbox-processor]] ADR for an example.
    16→
    17→2. **Experiments** (`experiments/`) — Hypothesis-driven logs capture what was tried, what happened, and what was learned. Failed experiments are as valuable as successful ones — they prevent repeating dead ends. See [[2026-02-07-ai-research-agent-for-vault-notes]] for an example.
    18→
    19→3. **Patterns** (`patterns/`) — Reusable solutions extracted from project work. When a problem is solved well, the solution is generalized and stored for future use, including code examples and guidance on when to apply it.
    20→
    21→## The Compounding Effect
    22→
    23→The value of the vault grows nonlinearly:
    24→
    25→- **Session 1** produces a few notes. The vault is a simple record.
    26→- **Session 10** has enough prior decisions that new work starts by checking what was already decided. Redundant research is eliminated.
    27→- **Session 100** has a rich web of cross-linked decisions, experiments, and patterns. New projects begin with relevant context automatically surfaced. The vault becomes an institutional memory that survives context windows, session boundaries, and team changes.
    28→
    29→## Role in the Cohezion Vault
    30→
    31→The Cohezion vault is built around compound engineering. The Cloud Vault MCP Server exposes this workflow programmatically through three operation layers:
    32→
    33→- **`VaultOps`** — Core read/write/search operations on the vault filesystem
    34→- **`CompoundOps`** — Structured logging of decisions, experiments, and patterns with enforced frontmatter schemas
    35→- **`ObsidianOps`** — Cross-linking via backlinks, tags, and wiki-links that connect knowledge across directories
    36→
    37→The `inbox/` directory serves as the entry point: raw ideas are captured quickly, then processed into the appropriate permanent directory. The proposed [[2026-02-07-event-driven-inbox-processor|inbox processor daemon]] would automate this flow, using AI to classify and structure incoming notes.
    38→
    39→## Relationship to AI-Assisted Engineering
    40→
    41→Compound engineering is especially powerful when combined with AI agents:
    42→
    43→- Agents can **read** prior decisions and patterns before starting new work, avoiding known pitfalls
    44→- Agents can **write** structured records of their own decisions and discoveries, contributing to the vault
    45→- The vault provides **persistent memory** that spans across context windows and sessions — solving the "blank slate" problem where each AI conversation starts from zero
    46→
    47→The [[2026-02-07-ai-research-agent-for-vault-notes|research agent experiment]] demonstrated that AI agents can autonomously produce vault-quality content, validating the compound engineering workflow end-to-end.
    48→
    49→## Primary Sources
    50→
    51→- Andrew S. Grove (1983). *High Output Management*. [https://www.amazon.com/High-Output-Management-Andrew-Grove/dp/0679762884](https://www.amazon.com/High-Output-Management-Andrew-Grove/dp/0679762884) — Grove's principle that strategic decisions made early disproportionately affect organizational leverage; early planning pays off 10x
    52→- Communications of the ACM (2024). *Knowledge Management with Patterns*. [https://cacm.acm.org/research/knowledge-management-with-patterns/](https://cacm.acm.org/research/knowledge-management-with-patterns/)
    53→- Lifecycle Insights (2024). *Engineering Knowledge Management*. [https://lifecycleinsights.com/tech-guide/engineering-knowledge-management](https://lifecycleinsights.com/tech-guide/engineering-knowledge-management)
    54→
    55→## Core Principles

    58→2. **Token Efficiency**: [[token-efficiency]] — Optimize LLM token consumption to maximize output per token spent
    59→3. **Template Reuse**: [[template-reuse]] — Copy working patterns (87% token savings) instead of building from scratch
    60→4. **Meta-Learning**: [[meta-learning]] — Extract lessons from failures (7.6x → 757x ROI over 100 projects)
