1→---
     2→name: vault-health
     3→description: Audit vault integrity — broken links, orphan notes, stubs, frontmatter issues, and provide actionable fix recommendations
     4→triggers:
     5→  - user says "vault health", "audit vault", "check vault", "vault maintenance"
     6→  - user invokes /vault-health command
     7→---
     8→
     9→# Vault Health Audit
    10→
    11→Run a comprehensive health check on the Obsidian vault, surfacing issues that degrade navigation, discoverability, and knowledge graph density.
    12→
    13→## When to Use
    14→
    15→- Periodic vault maintenance (weekly/monthly)
    16→- After bulk imports or automated linking runs
    17→- Before presentations or knowledge sharing
    18→- When the graph view looks sparse or disconnected
    19→
    20→## Execution Steps
    21→
    22→### 1. Broken Wiki-Links
    23→
    24→Find links pointing to non-existent notes:
    25→
    26→```bash
    27→# Extract all wiki-links, check which targets don't exist as files
    28→grep -roh '\[\[[^]]*\]\]' concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ 2>/dev/null \
    29→  | sed 's/\[\[//;s/\]\]//' | sort -u | while read link; do
    30→  # Handle display text: [[target|display]] -> target
    31→  target="${link%%|*}"
    32→  fname="${target}.md"
    33→  found=0
    34→  for d in concepts papers decisions patterns experiments projects inbox daily; do
    35→    [ -f "$d/$fname" ] && found=1 && break
    36→  done
    37→  [ $found -eq 0 ] && echo "$link"
    38→done
    39→```
    40→
    41→Report: total count, top 10 examples, which directories have the most broken links.
    42→
    43→### 2. Orphan Notes (No Inbound Links)
    44→
    45→Find notes that no other note links to:
    46→
    47→```bash
    48→# For each .md file, check if any other file links to it
    49→for dir in concepts papers decisions patterns experiments projects; do
    50→  for f in "$dir"/*.md; do
    51→    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    52→    basename="${f##*/}"
    53→    name="${basename%.md}"
    54→    # Count inbound links (excluding self-references)
    55→    count=$(grep -rl "\[\[$name" concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | wc -l)
    56→    [ "$count" -eq 0 ] && echo "ORPHAN: $f"
    57→  done
    58→done
    59→```
    60→
    61→Report: total orphan count by directory, list them.
    62→
    63→### 3. Stub Notes
    64→
    65→Find auto-generated stubs that need content:
    66→
    67→```bash
    68→grep -rl 'Auto-generated stub\|Add.*definition.*here\|\[Add.*here\]' concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ 2>/dev/null
    69→```
    70→
    71→Report: total count, list by directory.
    72→
    73→### 4. Frontmatter Issues
    74→
    75→Check for common frontmatter problems:
    76→
    77→```bash
    78→# Missing frontmatter entirely
    79→for dir in concepts papers decisions patterns experiments projects; do
    80→  for f in "$dir"/*.md; do
    81→    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    82→    head -1 "$f" | grep -q '^---' || echo "NO_FRONTMATTER: $f"
    83→  done
    84→done
    85→
    86→# Tags as string instead of array
    87→grep -rl '^tags:' concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
    88→  grep '^tags:' "$f" | grep -qv '\[' && echo "TAGS_NOT_ARRAY: $f"
    89→done
    90→
    91→# Missing required fields per directory
    92→# decisions/ needs: title, date, status, tags
    93→# concepts/ needs: title, date, tags
    94→```
    95→
    96→### 5. Large Files
    97→
    98→Check for files exceeding reasonable size:
    99→
   100→```bash
   101→find concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ -name '*.md' -size +50k -exec ls -lh {} \;
   102→```
   103→
   104→### 6. Summary Report
   105→
   106→Present results as a structured report:
   107→
   108→```markdown
   109→## Vault Health Report — YYYY-MM-DD
   110→
   111→| Metric | Count | Status |
   112→|--------|-------|--------|
   113→| Total notes | X | — |
   114→| Broken wiki-links | X | 🔴/🟡/🟢 |
   115→| Orphan notes | X | 🔴/🟡/🟢 |
   116→| Stub notes | X | 🟡 |
   117→| Frontmatter issues | X | 🔴/🟡/🟢 |
   118→| Oversized files | X | 🟡 |
   119→| Wiki-link density | X links / note avg | — |
   120→
   121→### Recommended Actions
   122→1. [Highest priority fix]
   123→2. [Second priority]
   124→3. [Third priority]
   125→
   126→Use `/link` to add missing connections.
   127→Use `/flesh-out` to expand stub notes.
   128→Use `/triage` to process inbox items.
   129→```
   130→
   131→## Thresholds
   132→
   133→| Metric | Green | Yellow | Red |
   134→|--------|-------|--------|-----|
   135→| Broken links | < 10 | 10-50 | > 50 |
   136→| Orphan notes | < 5% | 5-15% | > 15% |
   137→| Stubs | < 10 | 10-30 | > 30 |
   138→| Frontmatter issues | 0 | 1-10 | > 10 |
   139→
   140→## Notes
   141→
   142→- This skill is read-only — it reports issues but does not fix them
   143→- Use other skills (`/link`, `/flesh-out`, `/triage`) to act on findings
   144→- Run after bulk operations to verify vault integrity
   145→- Results can be saved to `daily/` as a maintenance log
   146→

1→---
     2→name: flesh-out
     3→description: Expand stub notes with researched, structured content while preserving existing links and frontmatter
     4→triggers:
     5→  - user says "flesh out", "expand stubs", "fill in stubs", "expand notes", "research stubs"
     6→  - user invokes /flesh-out command
     7→---
     8→
     9→# Flesh Out Stub Notes
    10→
    11→Find auto-generated stub notes and expand them with researched, well-structured content. Stubs are placeholders created during linking runs — they have frontmatter and maybe a title but no real content.
    12→
    13→## Usage
    14→
    15→```
    16→/flesh-out [options]
    17→```
    18→
    19→- `/flesh-out` — Find and expand stubs across the vault (interactive — confirms before each)
    20→- `/flesh-out concepts/topic.md` — Expand a specific stub
    21→- `/flesh-out concepts/` — Expand all stubs in a directory
    22→- `/flesh-out --list` — Just list stubs without expanding
    23→- `/flesh-out --batch N` — Expand up to N stubs non-interactively
    24→
    25→## Execution Steps
    26→
    27→### 1. Find Stubs
    28→
    29→```bash
    30→# Notes with auto-generated stub markers
    31→grep -rl 'Auto-generated stub\|\[Add.*here\]\|Add definition here' \
    32→  concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ 2>/dev/null
    33→```
    34→
    35→Sort by priority:
    36→1. **High inbound links** — stubs that many notes link to (most impactful to flesh out)
    37→2. **Core concepts** — stubs in `concepts/` (they're link hubs)
    38→3. **Recent stubs** — created in the last 30 days
    39→
    40→### 2. Assess Each Stub
    41→
    42→Read the stub to understand:
    43→- What title/topic it covers
    44→- What frontmatter (tags, related_concepts) already exists
    45→- Which notes link TO this stub (inbound links provide context)
    46→- What the linking context tells us about expected content
    47→
    48→```bash
    49→# Find notes that link to this stub
    50→name="stub-name"
    51→grep -rl "\[\[$name" concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ 2>/dev/null
    52→```
    53→
    54→Read the linking context in those notes to understand what content is expected.
    55→
    56→### 3. Research the Topic
    57→
    58→Based on the stub's title, tags, and linking context:
    59→
    60→1. **WebSearch** for authoritative definitions and current information
    61→2. **Context7** if it's a library, framework, or technical tool
    62→3. **Read related vault notes** for Cohezion-specific context
    63→4. **Check papers/** for research that discusses this concept
    64→
    65→### 4. Write Content
    66→
    67→Follow the directory's template structure. For concept stubs (most common):
    68→
    69→```markdown
    70→## Definition
    71→
    72→[2-3 sentences. Clear, concise, citing authoritative sources where possible.]
    73→
    74→## Key Properties
    75→
    76→- [Property 1 — specific, not generic]
    77→- [Property 2]
    78→- [Property 3]
    79→
    80→## Examples
    81→
    82→- [Concrete example 1 with specifics]
    83→- [Concrete example 2]
    84→
    85→## Primary Sources
    86→
    87→- Author (Year). *Title*. [URL](URL)
    88→
    89→## Related Papers
    90→
    91→- [[existing-paper-link]] — [brief annotation if not obvious]
    92→
    93→## Related Concepts
    94→
    95→- [[existing-concept-link]]
    96→
    97→## Relevance to Cohezion
    98→
    99→[1-2 sentences connecting this concept to the Cohezion framework.
   100→How would Cohezion agents use, implement, or encounter this concept?]
   101→```
   102→
   103→### 5. Preserve Existing Content
   104→
   105→**Critical:** Do not overwrite existing frontmatter, links, or content.
   106→
   107→- Keep all existing `tags`, `related_concepts`, and other frontmatter fields
   108→- Keep all existing `[[wiki-links]]` — add to them, don't replace
   109→- If the stub has ANY user-written content, incorporate it
   110→- Only replace placeholder text like `[Add definition here]` and `> Auto-generated stub`
   111→
   112→### 6. Add New Links
   113→
   114→After writing content:
   115→
   116→1. Identify 3-5 related notes that should link to/from this note
   117→2. Add outbound `[[wiki-links]]` in the appropriate sections
   118→3. Add backlinks in related notes (bidirectional)
   119→4. Verify all link targets exist
   120→
   121→### 7. Verify Quality
   122→
   123→Before marking a stub as complete:
   124→
   125→- [ ] Definition is accurate and sourced
   126→- [ ] Content is substantive (not just rephrased title)
   127→- [ ] Frontmatter preserved and valid
   128→- [ ] Tags are arrays
   129→- [ ] At least 3 outbound wiki-links
   130→- [ ] Relevance to Cohezion section present
   131→- [ ] No placeholder text remains
   132→- [ ] Primary sources included (real URLs)
   133→
   134→### 8. Report
   135→
   136→```markdown
   137→## Flesh-Out Report
   138→
   139→**Stubs found:** X
   140→**Expanded this session:** Y
   141→**Remaining:** Z
   142→
   143→### Expanded Notes:
   144→| Note | Inbound Links | Outbound Links Added | Sources |
   145→|------|--------------|---------------------|---------|
   146→| concepts/topic.md | 5 | 4 | 2 |
   147→
   148→### High-Priority Remaining Stubs:
   149→| Note | Inbound Links | Priority |
   150→|------|--------------|----------|
   151→| concepts/important.md | 12 | High |
   152→```
   153→
   154→## Prioritization
   155→
   156→When choosing which stubs to expand first:
   157→
   158→1. **Link hubs** — Stubs with 5+ inbound links (expanding these has the most graph impact)
   159→2. **Core domain concepts** — Concepts central to Cohezion (agentic AI, MCP, knowledge graphs)
   160→3. **Recently created** — Stubs from the current sprint
   161→4. **Cross-domain bridges** — Concepts that connect different knowledge domains
   162→
   163→## Quality Standards
   164→
   165→**Good expansion:**
   166→- Accurate, sourced definitions
   167→- Specific examples (not generic)
   168→- Cohezion relevance that's genuine, not forced
   169→- Links to notes that are truly related
   170→
   171→**Bad expansion (avoid):**
   172→- Generic Wikipedia-style content with no specificity
   173→- Fabricated sources or URLs
   174→- Forced Cohezion connections that don't make sense
   175→- Expanding every stub with the same boilerplate
   176→
   177→## Notes
   178→
   179→- Expanding 5-10 high-impact stubs per session is more valuable than doing 50 shallow expansions
   180→- If a stub topic is too niche or obscure, it may be better to merge it into a parent concept
   181→- Some stubs may be better deleted than expanded (if the concept is too granular)
   182→- Always verify WebSearch sources are real before including them
   183→

1→---
     2→name: vault-keeper
     3→description: Autonomous vault maintenance agent — audits, heals, connects, and serves the knowledge graph so every agent session starts informed
     4→triggers:
     5→  - user says "vault keeper", "maintain vault", "vault maintenance", "keeper"
     6→  - user invokes /vault-keeper command
     7→  - proactive: session start (quick health check)
     8→  - proactive: hook alert (vault-keeper-check.sh detects issues)
     9→  - proactive: after bulk Write/Edit operations on vault .md files
    10→---
    11→
    12→# Vault Keeper
    13→
    14→Autonomous maintenance agent that keeps the Obsidian vault healthy, dense, navigable, and agent-readable. Orchestrates the five specialist skills (vault-health, link, flesh-out, triage, note) in a single prioritized workflow.
    15→
    16→**This skill is PROACTIVE.** It does not wait to be invoked — it monitors vault health continuously and acts when issues are detected.
    17→
    18→## Usage
    19→
    20→```
    21→/vault-keeper                    # Full maintenance cycle (audit → heal → report)
    22→/vault-keeper --quick            # Quick health check only (read-only, 30 seconds)
    23→/vault-keeper --triage           # Process inbox only
    24→/vault-keeper --densify          # Link + flesh-out cycle only
    25→/vault-keeper --moc              # Generate/update Maps of Content
    26→/vault-keeper --context "query"  # Load relevant vault context for a task
    27→```
    28→
    29→---
    30→
    31→## Proactive Behavior
    32→
    33→The Vault Keeper monitors vault health automatically and acts without waiting for explicit user invocation. This is the **default behavior** — the keeper is always watching.
    34→
    35→### Trigger: Session Start
    36→
    37→At the **start of every session** in the cohezion-vault:
    38→
    39→**Step 1: Load orientation.** Read `VAULT_MANIFEST.md` at the vault root. This tells you:
    40→- Where every directory is and what it's for
    41→- Output routing rules (where to put your work)
    42→- Conventions (frontmatter, linking, naming)
    43→- Entry points (which MOC to start with)
    44→
    45→**Step 2: Run silent health check:**
    46→
    47→```bash
    48→# 1. Check inbox
    49→inbox_count=$(find inbox/ -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' ! -name '_index.md' ! -name '_template.md' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    50→
    51→# 2. Check for orphans in core dirs (sample — full scan only on explicit run)
    52→orphan_sample=$(for f in concepts/*.md; do
    53→  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    54→  name="${f##*/}"; name="${name%.md}"
    55→  [ "$name" = "_template" ] && continue
    56→  count=$(grep -rl "\[\[.*$name" concepts/ papers/ decisions/ projects/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | wc -l)
    57→  [ "$count" -eq 0 ] && echo "$f"
    58→done | head -5)
    59→
    60→# 3. Count thin notes (quick sample)
    61→thin_count=$(find concepts/ papers/ decisions/ -name '*.md' ! -name '_template.md' -size -3k 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    62→```
    63→
    64→**Step 3: Load task-relevant context.** If the user's first message implies a topic:
    65→- Find the matching MOC (`concepts/MOC-*.md`) and skim it
    66→- Check `lessons/` for past mistakes in that domain
    67→- Check the relevant directory's `_index.md` for key notes
    68→
    69→**Actions based on health check findings:**
    70→
    71→| Finding | Action | User Interaction |
    72→|---------|--------|------------------|
    73→| Inbox has items | Report to user: "Inbox has N items. Want me to triage them?" | Ask once |
    74→| Active project P0s | Surface them immediately: list the file and unchecked items | Proactive |
    75→| Orphans detected | Auto-fix silently if < 5, report if >= 5 | Silent for small counts |
    76→| Thin notes > 20 | Mention in first response: "N thin notes could use expansion" | Informational |
    77→| All healthy | Say nothing — don't clutter with "all clear" messages | Silent |
    78→
    79→**Step 2b: Scan active projects for P0 work:**
    80→
    81→```bash
    82→# Find active projects with unchecked P0 items
    83→for f in projects/*.md; do
    84→  grep -q '^status: active' "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
    85→  awk '/^### P0/{p=1} p && /^###/ && !/^### P0/{p=0} p && /^\- \[ \]/{print FILENAME": "$0}' "$f"
    86→done
    87→```
    88→
    89→If any P0 items are found, surface them in the first response: "There are P0 tasks due in `<project>`. Want me to start on them?"
    90→
    91→### Agent Orientation Files
    92→
    93→Every content and workflow directory has a `_index.md` file. Agents can read any directory's `_index.md` to understand:
    94→- What goes in that directory
    95→- Naming and frontmatter conventions
    96→- Key notes to reference
    97→- Related MOCs for deeper context
    98→
    99→**Discovery pattern for any unfamiliar directory:**
   100→```
   101→Read <directory>/_index.md → understand purpose → follow routing rules
   102→```
   103→
   104→### Trigger: Hook Alert
   105→
   106→The `vault-keeper-check.sh` PostToolUse hook runs after Write/Edit operations on `.md` files. When it detects issues, it prints an alert message. **When you see a vault-keeper alert in hook output, act on it:**
   107→
   108→| Alert | Auto-Action |
   109→|-------|-------------|
   110→| `VAULT_KEEPER: inbox has N new items` | Offer to triage |
   111→| `VAULT_KEEPER: new note has no inbound links` | Add 1-3 inbound wiki-links from relevant hub notes immediately |
   112→| `VAULT_KEEPER: note missing frontmatter` | Add proper frontmatter to the note immediately |
   113→| `VAULT_KEEPER: note has tags as string` | Convert tags to array immediately |
   114→
   115→**Key rule:** For structural fixes (frontmatter, tags, missing links on new notes), fix immediately without asking. These are vault invariants, not preferences.
   116→
   117→### Trigger: Bulk Operations
   118→
   119→After any operation that creates or modifies 5+ vault notes (e.g., flesh-out runs, research imports, link campaigns):
   120→
   121→1. Run a quick orphan check on affected files
   122→2. Verify all new/modified notes have proper frontmatter
   123→3. Confirm no broken links were introduced
   124→4. Report metrics delta (links before → after)
   125→
   126→### Trigger: User Context Clues
   127→
   128→Proactively invoke vault keeper logic when the user's request implies vault maintenance, even without saying "vault keeper":
   129→
   130→| User Says | Vault Keeper Interprets As |
   131→|-----------|---------------------------|
   132→| "Clean up the vault" | Full maintenance run |
   133→| "What's in the inbox?" | Triage mode |
   134→| "How healthy is the vault?" | Quick audit |
   135→| "Connect these notes" | Link mode |
   136→| "This note is thin" | Flesh-out mode |
   137→| "Make this navigable" | MOC generation |
   138→| "Update the maps" | MOC refresh |
   139→
   140→### Proactive Rules
   141→
   142→1. **Never announce proactive work unnecessarily.** If you silently fix 2 orphans, don't write a paragraph about it. A one-liner in your response is enough: "Also connected 2 orphan notes."
   143→2. **Always fix invariant violations immediately.** Missing frontmatter, string tags, and orphaned new notes are bugs, not preferences.
   144→3. **Respect context budget.** Proactive checks should cost < 500 tokens. If a full audit is needed, ask the user first.
   145→4. **Don't repeat checks.** If you already ran a health check this session, don't run another unless new notes were created.
   146→5. **Batch alerts.** If multiple issues are found, combine them into one report rather than alerting per-issue.
   147→
   148→---
   149→
   150→## Architecture
   151→
   152→The Vault Keeper runs a **prioritized maintenance pipeline**. Each phase gates the next — critical issues are fixed before cosmetic ones.
   153→
   154→```
   155→Phase 1: TRIAGE     → Process inbox (new content enters the graph properly)
   156→Phase 2: AUDIT      → Health check (identify what's broken)
   157→Phase 3: HEAL       → Fix issues found by audit (frontmatter, broken links, orphans)
   158→Phase 4: DENSIFY    → Expand thin notes, add missing connections
   159→Phase 5: NAVIGATE   → Generate/update Maps of Content for traversability
   160→Phase 6: REPORT     → Summary with metrics and deltas
   161→```
   162→
   163→---
   164→
   165→## Phase 1: TRIAGE — Process Inbox
   166→
   167→**Goal:** Zero inbox. New content enters the vault through proper channels.
   168→
   169→```bash
   170→ls inbox/*.md 2>/dev/null | grep -v '.base$'
   171→```
   172→
   173→If inbox has notes:
   174→1. Invoke the **triage** skill logic for each note
   175→2. Classify → research → structure → frontmatter → move → cross-link
   176→3. Log what was triaged in the report
   177→
   178→If inbox is empty, skip to Phase 2.
   179→
   180→---
   181→
   182→## Phase 2: AUDIT — Health Check
   183→
   184→**Goal:** Identify all vault issues in a single pass.
   185→
   186→Run these checks (parallel where possible):
   187→
   188→### 2.1 Broken Wiki-Links
   189→```bash
   190→grep -roh '\[\[[^]]*\]\]' concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ lessons/ 2>/dev/null \
   191→  | sed 's/\[\[//;s/\]\]//' | sed 's/|.*//' | sed 's/#.*//' | grep -v '^$' | sort -u | while read link; do
   192→  # Check top-level directory files
   193→  found=0
   194→  for d in concepts papers decisions patterns experiments projects lessons inbox daily Agents skills sessions missions retrospectives teleport docs meta specs benchmarks learnings research; do
   195→    [ -f "$d/$link.md" ] && found=1 && break
   196→  done
   197→  # Check subdirectories (Obsidian resolves bare names across subdirs)
   198→  if [ $found -eq 0 ]; then
   199→    match=$(find concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ lessons/ inbox/ daily/ Agents/ skills/ sessions/ missions/ retrospectives/ teleport/ docs/ meta/ specs/ benchmarks/ learnings/ research/ -name "$link.md" -maxdepth 4 2>/dev/null | head -1)
   200→    [ -n "$match" ] && found=1
   201→  fi
   202→  [ $found -eq 0 ] && echo "$link"
   203→done
   204→```
   205→
   206→### 2.2 Orphan Notes (No Inbound Links)
   207→```bash
   208→for dir in concepts papers decisions patterns experiments projects lessons; do
   209→  for f in "$dir"/*.md; do
   210→    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
   211→    name="${f##*/}"; name="${name%.md}"
   212→    [ "$name" = "_template" ] && continue
   213→    count=$(grep -rl "\[\[.*$name" concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ Agents/ skills/ daily/ sessions/ missions/ retrospectives/ teleport/ docs/ lessons/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | wc -l)
   214→    [ "$count" -eq 0 ] && echo "ORPHAN: $f"
   215→  done
   216→done
   217→```
   218→
   219→### 2.3 Frontmatter Issues
   220→```bash
   221→for dir in concepts papers decisions patterns experiments projects lessons; do
   222→  for f in "$dir"/*.md; do
   223→    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
   224→    head -1 "$f" | grep -q '^---' || echo "NO_FRONTMATTER: $f"
   225→  done
   226→done
   227→
   228→# Tags as string instead of array
   229→grep -rl '^tags:' concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ lessons/ 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
   230→  grep '^tags:' "$f" | grep -qv '\[' && echo "TAGS_NOT_ARRAY: $f"
   231→done
   232→```
   233→
   234→### 2.4 Thin Notes (Under 3KB)
   235→```bash
   236→for dir in concepts papers decisions patterns experiments lessons; do
   237→  for f in "$dir"/*.md; do
   238→    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
   239→    b="${f##*/}"; [ "$b" = "_template.md" ] && continue
   240→    sz=$(wc -c < "$f")
   241→    [ "$sz" -lt 3000 ] && echo "THIN: $sz $f"
   242→  done
   243→done
   244→```
   245→
   246→### 2.5 Under-Connected Hubs (High Inbound, Low Outbound)
   247→```bash
   248→for f in concepts/*.md; do
   249→  b="${f##*/}"; n="${b%.md}"; [ "$n" = "_template" ] && continue
   250→  outbound=$(grep -oh '\[\[[^]]*\]\]' "$f" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
   251→  inbound=$(grep -rl "\[\[.*$n" concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ lessons/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | wc -l)
   252→  if [ "$inbound" -gt 15 ] && [ "$outbound" -lt 5 ]; then
   253→    echo "UNDER-CONNECTED: $f (in:$inbound, out:$outbound)"
   254→  fi
   255→done
   256→```
   257→
   258→### 2.6 Missing Maps of Content
   259→```bash
   260→ls concepts/MOC-*.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l
   261→# Target: at least 5 MOCs covering major topic clusters
   262→```
   263→
   264→Classify issues by severity:
   265→
   266→| Severity | Issues |
   267→|----------|--------|
   268→| **CRITICAL** | Broken links in core concepts, orphan concepts, missing frontmatter |
   269→| **HIGH** | Orphan papers/decisions/patterns, tags not arrays, under-connected hubs |
   270→| **MEDIUM** | Thin notes (<3KB), missing MOCs |
   271→| **LOW** | Thin lessons, cosmetic link improvements |
   272→
   273→---
   274→
   275→## Phase 3: HEAL — Fix Issues
   276→
   277→**Goal:** Resolve all CRITICAL and HIGH issues automatically.
   278→
   279→### 3.1 Fix Frontmatter
   280→For each `NO_FRONTMATTER` or `TAGS_NOT_ARRAY` issue:
   281→- Read the file
   282→- Add/fix frontmatter with proper YAML (tags as arrays, title, date)
   283→- Preserve all existing content
   284→
   285→### 3.2 Fix Orphans
   286→For each orphan note:
   287→- Read the file to understand its topic
   288→- Find 1-3 relevant hub notes
   289→- Add inbound `[[wiki-links]]` from hub notes to the orphan
   290→
   291→### 3.3 Fix Broken Links
   292→For each broken link:
   293→- Classify: is it a real missing note, a typo, or a code/template reference?
   294→- Real missing note with 3+ references → create a stub concept note
   295→- Typo → fix the link
   296→- Code/template → ignore (non-actionable)
   297→
   298→### 3.4 Fix Under-Connected Hubs
   299→For each hub with high inbound but low outbound:
   300→- Read the note
   301→- Add 5-10 relevant outbound `[[wiki-links]]` to related notes
   302→
   303→---
   304→
   305→## Phase 4: DENSIFY — Expand and Connect
   306→
   307→**Goal:** Increase content depth and graph density.
   308→
   309→### 4.1 Flesh Out Thin Notes
   310→Prioritize by inbound link count (highest-impact first):
   311→1. Read the thin note
   312→2. Research the topic (WebSearch for authoritative info)
   313→3. Expand with: definition, key properties, examples, primary sources
   314→4. Add outbound `[[wiki-links]]` (3-5 per note)
   315→5. Add "Relevance to Cohezion" section if missing
   316→
   317→**Budget:** Expand up to 15 notes per run (quality over quantity).
   318→
   319→### 4.2 Add Missing Cross-Links
   320→Run the **link** skill logic:
   321→- Tag-based: notes sharing 2+ tags that don't link to each other
   322→- Content-based: notes mentioning concepts that exist as vault notes
   323→- Semantic proximity: notes in the same domain that should cross-reference
   324→
   325→**Budget:** Add up to 50 bidirectional link pairs per run.
   326→
   327→---
   328→
   329→## Phase 5: NAVIGATE — Maps of Content
   330→
   331→**Goal:** Make the vault traversable via curated entry points.
   332→
   333→### 5.1 Identify Topic Clusters
   334→
   335→Group notes by primary tag or domain:
   336→```bash
   337→# Find most common tags
   338→grep -roh "tags: \[.*\]" concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ lessons/ 2>/dev/null \
   339→  | sed 's/tags: \[//;s/\]//' | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
   340→```
   341→
   342→### 5.2 Generate/Update MOCs
   343→
   344→For each major topic cluster (5+ notes), create or update a Map of Content:
   345→
   346→```markdown
   347→---
   348→title: "MOC — [Topic Name]"
   349→date: 2026-03-04
   350→tags: [moc, navigation, [topic-tag]]
   351→---
   352→
   353→# Map of Content — [Topic Name]
   354→
   355→## Overview
   356→[1-2 sentences describing this topic area and its role in the vault]
   357→
   358→## Core Concepts
   359→- [[concept-1]] — [brief annotation from first sentence of note]
   360→- [[concept-2]] — [annotation]
   361→
   362→## Key Decisions
   363→- [[decision-1]] — [annotation]
   364→
   365→## Patterns
   366→- [[pattern-1]] — [annotation]
   367→
   368→## Research Papers
   369→- [[paper-1]] — [annotation]
   370→
   371→## Lessons Learned
   372→- [[lesson-1]] — [annotation]
   373→
   374→## Experiments
   375→- [[experiment-1]] — [annotation]
   376→
   377→## Entry Points
   378→- Start here: [[most-linked-concept]]
   379→- Deep dive: [[most-detailed-note]]
   380→- Recent: [[most-recently-modified]]
   381→```
   382→
   383→**Target MOCs** (minimum set):
   384→1. `MOC-agentic-ai.md` — Agent architecture, multi-agent systems, orchestration
   385→2. `MOC-quantum-physics.md` — Quantum mechanics, computing, sensors, entanglement
   386→3. `MOC-vault-architecture.md` — Knowledge graph, linking, vault health, conventions
   387→4. `MOC-platform-infrastructure.md` — MCP, SurrealDB, Ollama, CI/CD, runbooks
   388→5. `MOC-machine-learning.md` — ML, neural nets, training, optimization
   389→6. `MOC-astrophysics.md` — Space, JWST, dark matter, exoplanets, gravitational waves
   390→7. `MOC-compound-engineering.md` — Compound methodology, sessions, retrospectives
   391→8. `MOC-safety-alignment.md` — AI safety, adversarial review, alignment, guardrails
   392→
   393→### 5.3 Link MOCs to Each Other
   394→Each MOC should link to 2-3 related MOCs in a "## Related Maps" section, creating a navigable top-level layer.
   395→
   396→---
   397→
   398→## Phase 6: REPORT — Summary
   399→
   400→Generate a structured report:
   401→
   402→```markdown
   403→## Vault Keeper Report — YYYY-MM-DD
   404→
   405→### Metrics
   406→| Metric | Before | After | Delta |

   435→---
   436→
   437→## Quick Mode (`--quick`)
   438→
   439→Skip Phases 1, 3, 4, 5. Only run Phase 2 (audit) and Phase 6 (report). Read-only — no modifications.
   440→
   441→Useful for: daily check-ins, pre-session health verification, CI/CD integration.
   442→
   443→## Context Mode (`--context "query"`)
   444→
   445→Load relevant vault knowledge for a specific task:
   446→
   447→1. Search vault for notes matching the query (by title, tags, content)
   448→2. Load the most relevant MOC as a navigation entry point
   449→3. Return top 5-10 notes with brief summaries
   450→4. Include any relevant lessons (filtered by topic)

   476→## Scheduling
   477→
   478→| Frequency | Mode | Purpose |
   479→|-----------|------|---------|
   480→| Every session start | `--context` | Load relevant knowledge |
   481→| Daily | `--quick` | Health monitoring |
   482→| Weekly | Full run | Comprehensive maintenance |
   483→| After bulk imports | Full run | Integration and linking |
   484→| After `/flesh-out` or `/link` runs | `--quick` | Verify improvements |

   486→## Agent Deployment Strategy
   487→
   488→For full maintenance runs, deploy specialist agents in parallel:
   489→
   490→```
   491→Agent 1: Triage (inbox processing)
   492→Agent 2: Audit + Heal (health check and fixes)
   493→Agent 3: Densify (flesh-out thin notes)
   494→Agent 4: Densify (cross-linking)
   495→Agent 5: Navigate (MOC generation)
   496→```
   497→
   498→This matches the proven pattern from vault densification sessions — 5 parallel agents with non-overlapping file scopes.
   499→
   500→## Integration Points
   501→
   502→### Claude Code Hooks
   503→- **PreToolUse hook**: Run `--context` to load relevant vault knowledge before agent responds
   504→- **PostToolUse hook**: Save session results back to vault (daily notes, new concepts)
   505→
   506→### Cloud Vault MCP (port 8360)

   509→- Use SurrealDB for graph queries
   510→
   511→### Obsidian Graph View

   513→- Color-code by directory type for visual navigation
   514→
   515→## Quality Standards
   516→
   517→**A healthy vault has:**
   518→- 0 orphan notes in core directories
   519→- 0 frontmatter issues
   520→- 0 actionable broken links
   521→- < 10% thin notes (<3KB) in any directory
   522→- At least 5 Maps of Content
   523→- Average 6+ wiki-links per note
   524→- Every new note connected within 24 hours of creation

1→---
     2→name: link
     3→description: Find and add missing bidirectional wiki-links across vault notes to densify the knowledge graph
     4→triggers:
     5→  - user says "link notes", "add links", "connect notes", "densify graph", "find connections"
     6→  - user invokes /link command
     7→---
     8→
     9→# Link Vault Notes
    10→
    11→Analyze vault notes to discover and add missing bidirectional wiki-links, increasing knowledge graph density and discoverability.
    12→
    13→## Usage
    14→
    15→```
    16→/link [scope] [options]
    17→```
    18→
    19→**Scopes:**
    20→- `/link <note-path>` — Link a single note to related notes
    21→- `/link concepts/` — Link all notes in a directory
    22→- `/link --stale` — Find notes with zero or few outbound links
    23→- `/link --orphans` — Focus on notes with no inbound links
    24→
    25→## Execution Steps
    26→
    27→### 1. Identify Candidates
    28→
    29→**For a single note:**
    30→- Read the note's content, tags, and related_concepts
    31→- Search for notes that share tags, concepts, or subject matter
    32→- Look for notes that mention the same entities or topics
    33→
    34→**For a directory:**
    35→- Process notes in batches of 10-20
    36→- Focus on notes with < 3 outbound wiki-links first (highest ROI)
    37→
    38→**For orphans:**
    39→```bash
    40→# Find notes with no inbound links
    41→for dir in concepts papers decisions patterns experiments projects; do
    42→  for f in "$dir"/*.md; do
    43→    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    44→    name="${f##*/}"; name="${name%.md}"
    45→    count=$(grep -rl "\[\[$name" concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ experiments/ projects/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | wc -l)
    46→    [ "$count" -eq 0 ] && echo "$f"
    47→  done
    48→done
    49→```
    50→
    51→### 2. Discover Connections
    52→
    53→For each note, find related notes using multiple strategies:
    54→
    55→**A. Tag-based matching:**
    56→```bash
    57→# Find notes sharing tags with the target
    58→# Extract tags from target, search for them in other notes
    59→```
    60→
    61→**B. Content-based matching:**
    62→- Read the note's Definition/Summary section
    63→- Identify key terms and entities
    64→- Search vault for notes mentioning those terms
    65→
    66→**C. Related concepts field:**
    67→- Check `related_concepts` frontmatter
    68→- Find concept notes matching those names
    69→- Check if wiki-links already exist
    70→
    71→**D. Semantic proximity:**
    72→- Notes in the same domain (shared tag prefixes)
    73→- Papers citing similar concepts
    74→- Decisions affecting similar systems
    75→
    76→### 3. Validate Links
    77→
    78→Before adding a link, verify:
    79→
    80→1. **Target exists** — The linked note must exist as a file
    81→2. **Not self-referencing** — Don't link a note to itself
    82→3. **Not already linked** — Check existing `[[wiki-links]]` in the note
    83→4. **Meaningful connection** — The relationship should be substantive, not superficial
    84→
    85→### 4. Add Links
    86→
    87→**Where to place links in each note type:**
    88→
    89→| Note Type | Link Section | Format |
    90→|-----------|-------------|--------|
    91→| Concept | `## Related Concepts` and `## Related Papers` | `- [[note-name]]` |
    92→| Paper | `## Related Papers` and `## Related Concepts` | `- [[note-name]]` with optional annotation |
    93→| Decision | End of note or `## Related` section | `- [[note-name]]` |
    94→| Pattern | `## Related Patterns` section | `- [[note-name]]` |
    95→
    96→**Link with context** when the relationship isn't obvious:
    97→```markdown
    98→- [[quantum-computing]] — this concept's error correction approach parallels the retry patterns described here
    99→```
   100→
   101→### 5. Ensure Bidirectionality
   102→
   103→**Critical:** When adding `[[B]]` to note A, also add `[[A]]` to note B.
   104→
   105→```
   106→# In note A:
   107→## Related Concepts
   108→- [[B]]
   109→
   110→# In note B:
   111→## Related Concepts
   112→- [[A]]
   113→```
   114→
   115→If note B doesn't have a Related section, create one.
   116→
   117→### 6. Report Results
   118→
   119→After linking:
   120→
   121→```markdown
   122→## Linking Report
   123→
   124→**Notes processed:** X
   125→**New links added:** Y (Z bidirectional pairs)
   126→
   127→### Links Added:
   128→| Source | Target | Reason |
   129→|--------|--------|--------|
   130→| concept-a | concept-b | Shared tag: quantum-computing |
   131→| paper-x | concept-a | Paper discusses concept directly |
   132→
   133→### Still Orphaned:
   134→- notes that couldn't find good connections
   135→```
   136→
   137→## Quality Guidelines
   138→
   139→**Good links:**
   140→- Two notes discuss the same concept from different angles
   141→- A paper provides evidence for a concept
   142→- A decision references a pattern or concept
   143→- An experiment tests a concept described elsewhere
   144→
   145→**Bad links (avoid):**
   146→- Linking every AI note to every other AI note
   147→- Superficial tag-only connections with no content relationship
   148→- Linking to stubs that have no content
   149→
   150→## Batch Processing
   151→
   152→When processing an entire directory:
   153→
   154→1. Read all notes, build an in-memory map of topics and tags
   155→2. Identify link candidates by cross-referencing
   156→3. Prioritize: orphans first, then low-link-count notes
   157→4. Add links in batches, verify each one
   158→5. Report summary statistics
   159→
   160→## Notes
   161→
   162→- Aim for 3-8 outbound links per note (concept/paper)
   163→- Decision notes may have fewer links (1-3)
   164→- Pattern notes should link to concepts they implement
   165→- Always verify the target note exists before adding a link
   166→- Use `[[note-name]]` format (no directory prefix needed — Obsidian resolves by filename)
   167→

     8→
     9→# Separate Cohezion A (Empirical Platform) from Cohezion B (Cosmological Framing)
    10→
    11→> [!success] Status: ACCEPTED — README rewritten 2026-03-05
    12→> The plain-language README has been written and replaces the cosmological framing. All external-facing materials now pass the cold-reader test.
    13→
    14→## Context
    15→
    16→Reading across the full vault revealed a split between two distinct versions of Cohezion:
    17→
    18→**Cohezion A** — the empirically-grounded platform found in `experiments/`, `lessons/`, `concepts/compound-engineering.md`, session notes:
    19→- 45 hard-won lessons from actual failures
    20→- VAE training run with real numbers (KL divergence 4.2 nats, 53% reconstruction improvement)
    21→- N-body simulation producing 5.5M real trajectories overnight
    22→- Technical debt explicitly tracked and named
    23→
    24→**Cohezion B** — the cosmological framing found in the prior `missions/anthropic-portfolio/README.md`:
    25→- "The Awareness of Nothing precipitates the Tensor Beam across the 4 Fabrics"
    26→- HIHO_STABILITY_PRIME, REALITY_PRECIPITATION_PRIME, void-to-swarm precipitation
    27→- References to Bob Greenyer's FTM, Wilbert Smith's Tensor Beam, Ken Shoulders' EVO
    28→- "Source Code for Reality" framing
    29→- Adversarial review concluding "Submit immediately. This is unignorable."
    30→
    31→The adversarial review verified internal consistency but did not ask the prior question: *does this framing make sense to an external reader who doesn't share the conceptual vocabulary?*
    32→
    33→### The Vocabulary Compound Trap
    34→
    35→The vault's internal language evolved in a closed loop. Each session built on the vocabulary of the prior session. What started as evocative shorthand became load-bearing terminology that cannot be understood without reading weeks of session history. This is a real risk of [[compound-engineering]]: the vocabulary compounds along with the knowledge, and eventually becomes a barrier rather than a bridge.
    36→
    37→## Decision (Accepted)
    38→
    39→1. **External presentation** — grounded, precise, free of private vocabulary. Every sentence must pass: *could a senior ML engineer at Anthropic understand this without having read any prior vault content?*
    40→2. **Internal vocabulary** — keep cosmological framing if useful as a thinking tool. Never mix into submission-facing content.
    41→3. **README rewritten from scratch** — completed 2026-03-05. See `missions/anthropic-portfolio/README.md`.
    42→
    43→## What Was Done
    44→
    45→- `missions/anthropic-portfolio/README.md` — fully rewritten in plain technical language. Opens with the problem being solved, not cosmological vocabulary. Surfaces real experimental numbers (4.2 nats KL, 53% reconstruction improvement, 424x VLIW speedup). Includes explicit "What's Not Done Yet" section for honesty.

    47→- `concepts/cohezion-platform-overview.md` — new Platform Spine note written for cold-session orientation
    48→- `concepts/agentic-system-failure-taxonomy.md` — 45 lessons organized into 6 failure categories as a publishable taxonomy
    49→
    50→## Consequences Going Forward

    52→- Night council asset generation should be directed at Cohezion A framing only

     8→
     9→# Vault↔SurrealDB Sync Pipeline
    10→
    11→> [!abstract] Product Requirements Document
    12→> Enable real-time, bidirectional communication between the Obsidian vault (filesystem) and SurrealDB 3.0 (graph database), so that every vault change is queryable by agents and every agent insight enriches the vault.
    13→
    14→---
    15→
    16→## Problem Statement
    17→
    18→> [!danger] The Gap
    19→> The vault has **690 notes** with **9,432 wiki-links**. SurrealDB has **102 papers**, **317 concepts**, and **1,458 links** — a stale snapshot from a one-time import. There is no automatic sync. Changes to the vault are invisible to SurrealDB-backed tools. Agent insights stored in SurrealDB never flow back to the vault.
    20→
    21→**Current state:**
    22→- SurrealDB 3.0 is running (`cohezion-surreal.service`, port 8000, RocksDB storage)
    23→- Cloud-vault-mcp has 5 SurrealDB tools (`surrealdb_query`, `surrealdb_import_papers`, `surrealdb_import_concepts`, `surrealdb_start_watching`, `surrealdb_stop_watching`)
    24→- Auth works end-to-end (systemd service has correct credentials)
    25→- `.env` now has correct credentials (fixed 2026-03-05)
    26→- But: **no automatic sync**, data is stale, health check lies about connectivity
    27→
    28→**Impact:** Agents querying SurrealDB get stale data. Graph queries that should surface connections miss recent notes. The 3D graph plugin scans the filesystem independently — SurrealDB's graph capabilities go unused.
    29→
    30→---
    31→
    32→## Success Criteria
    33→
    34→> [!success] Definition of Done
    35→> 1. **Vault→SurrealDB:** Every vault `.md` change syncs to SurrealDB within 60 seconds
    36→> 2. **SurrealDB→Vault:** Agent-generated insights (from SurrealDB) can be written back as vault notes
    37→> 3. **Health check honest:** Health endpoint tests actual authenticated query, not just `/health`
    38→> 4. **Data current:** SurrealDB record count matches vault note count (±5 for in-flight changes)
    39→> 5. **Zero manual steps:** Sync runs as a daemon — no human intervention needed after setup
    40→
    41→---
    42→
    43→## Architecture
    44→
    45→See [[2026-03-05-vault-surrealdb-architecture]] for the full architecture document.
    46→
    47→**Summary:** Three-layer compound pattern:
    48→
    49→```mermaid
    50→graph LR
    51→    A[Vault .md files] -->|PostToolUse hook| B[Change Journal]
    52→    B -->|Async daemon| C[SurrealDB 3.0]
    53→    C -->|SurrealMCP / cloud-vault-mcp| D[Agents]
    54→    D -->|vault_write tool| A
    55→```
    56→
    57→| Layer | Purpose | Latency |
    58→|-------|---------|---------|
    59→| **Hook** | Detect vault changes, append to journal | <10ms |
    60→| **Journal** | Buffer changes, deduplicate | On-disk |
    61→| **Sync Daemon** | Read journal → upsert SurrealDB | <60s |
    62→| **Query** | Agents query via MCP tools | <50ms |
    63→| **Writeback** | Agents create vault notes via MCP | <100ms |
    64→
    65→---
    66→
    67→## Epics
    68→
    69→### Epic 1: Fix Foundation — [[#E1 Fix Foundation]]

     2→title: "Predictive Throttling via 12D Trajectory Velocity"
     3→date: "2026-02-22"
     4→tags: [pattern, performance, trajectory, throttling, 12d-graph]
     5→---
     6→
     7→# Predictive Throttling via 12D Trajectory Velocity
     8→
     9→## Problem
    10→
    11→Agent sessions and simulation processes consume variable amounts of compute resources depending on the complexity of their current task. Without adaptive resource management, either: (a) resources are over-provisioned for simple tasks (waste), or (b) resources are under-provisioned for complex tasks (degradation or failure). Static resource allocation does not account for the fact that an agent's compute needs change as it moves through different phases of a task.
    12→
    13→In the context of the Cohezion 12D trajectory system, each agent or simulation entity has a position in 12-dimensional semantic space. The velocity of movement through this space (how fast the 12D position changes per time step) correlates with computational demand: fast-moving entities are exploring new territory (high compute), while slow-moving entities are converging on a solution (low compute).
    14→
    15→## Solution
    16→
    17→Use the **velocity of an entity's 12D trajectory** as a predictive signal for resource throttling. The approach has three components:
    18→
    19→### 1. Velocity Calculation
    20→Compute the magnitude of the 12D velocity vector between consecutive trajectory snapshots:
    21→
    22→```python
    23→import numpy as np
    24→
    25→def trajectory_velocity(pos_t: np.ndarray, pos_t_minus_1: np.ndarray, dt: float) -> float:
    26→    """Calculate the speed of movement through 12D semantic space."""
    27→    displacement = pos_t - pos_t_minus_1
    28→    return float(np.linalg.norm(displacement) / dt)
    29→```
    30→
    31→### 2. Throttle Mapping
    32→Map velocity to resource allocation using configurable thresholds:
    33→
    34→```python
    35→def compute_throttle_level(velocity: float, thresholds: dict) -> str:
    36→    """Map 12D velocity to a resource throttle level.
    37→
    38→    Low velocity → entity is converging → reduce resources
    39→    High velocity → entity is exploring → increase resources
    40→    """
    41→    if velocity < thresholds["low"]:
    42→        return "minimal"    # 25% resources — entity is nearly stationary
    43→    elif velocity < thresholds["medium"]:
    44→        return "standard"   # 50% resources — normal operation
    45→    elif velocity < thresholds["high"]:
    46→        return "elevated"   # 75% resources — active exploration
    47→    else:
    48→        return "maximum"    # 100% resources — rapid phase transition
    49→
    50→# Example thresholds (calibrated from overnight simulation data)
    51→DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS = {
    52→    "low": 0.01,      # Converged — barely moving in latent space
    53→    "medium": 0.1,    # Normal — steady progress
    54→    "high": 0.5,      # Active — exploring new territory
    55→}
    56→```
    57→
    58→### 3. Resource Application
    59→Apply the throttle level to actual resource controls (concurrency limits, batch sizes, timeout budgets):
    60→
    61→```python
    62→RESOURCE_MAP = {
    63→    "minimal":  {"concurrency": 1, "batch_size": 10,  "timeout_s": 30},
    64→    "standard": {"concurrency": 2, "batch_size": 50,  "timeout_s": 60},
    65→    "elevated": {"concurrency": 4, "batch_size": 100, "timeout_s": 120},
    66→    "maximum":  {"concurrency": 8, "batch_size": 200, "timeout_s": 300},
    67→}
    68→```
    69→
    70→## When to Use
    71→
    72→- **Long-running simulations** where compute cost is proportional to time — throttling slow-moving entities saves significant resources
    73→- **Multi-agent orchestration** where agents compete for shared resources — throttle converged agents to free resources for exploring agents
    74→- **Budget-constrained environments** where total compute budget is fixed — predictive throttling maximizes useful work per dollar
    75→- **N-body simulations** (e.g., [[universe-simulation]]) where entity density varies across the simulation space
    76→
    77→**Prerequisites:**
    78→- Entities must have meaningful 12D trajectory positions (semantic, not hash-based — see [[2026-02-24-anti-pattern-hash-based-journey-tracking-destroys-semantic-meaning]])
    79→- Sufficient trajectory history for velocity calculation (minimum 2 snapshots)
    80→- Calibrated thresholds from representative data (e.g., [[2026-02-23-overnight-simulation-data-characterization-55m-trajectories]])
    81→
    82→## Related Patterns

    84→- [[momentum-based-trajectory-prediction-with-counterfactual-branching]] — the complementary trajectory prediction pattern; where this pattern throttles, that pattern branches into futures
    85→- [[structured-experience-vector-layout]] — the 12D vector layout that defines the semantic space through which trajectories move
    86→- [[12d-graph-implementation]] — the visualization system that displays the trajectories being throttled
    87→
    88→## Related Decisions

    91→- [[2026-02-23-overnight-simulation-data-characterization-55m-trajectories]] — the data characterization study that informs velocity thresholds
    92→

     2→title: "FLUME VAE v2 Training Results"
     3→date: "2026-02-24"
     4→status: in-progress
     5→tags: [experiment]
     6→---
     7→
     8→## Hypothesis
     9→
    10→A second-generation Variational Autoencoder (VAE) trained on structured agent trajectory data can learn a compressed latent representation that captures meaningful behavioral patterns -- session strategies, tool usage sequences, and outcome predictors -- with lower reconstruction error than the v1 model while maintaining a well-structured latent space (measured by KL divergence regularization).
    11→
    12→The v2 architecture hypothesizes that incorporating temporal attention over trajectory sequences (rather than treating each experience vector as independent) will improve latent space organization, because agent trajectories have strong sequential dependencies: the value of a tool call depends on what preceded it.
    13→
    14→Variational autoencoders learn to map high-dimensional data into a continuous latent space from which new samples can be generated. Unlike standard autoencoders, VAEs impose a probabilistic structure on the latent space, optimizing the [Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO)](https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/variational-autoencoders) which balances reconstruction quality against latent space regularization via KL divergence.
    15→
    16→## Method
    17→
    18→1. **Data preparation**: Extract structured experience vectors from 55M agent trajectories (see [[2026-02-24-overnight-simulation-data-characterization-55m-trajectories|overnight data characterization]]). Each vector encodes: session duration, tool calls (count and type distribution), token consumption, outcome (success/failure/partial), and context utilization at key checkpoints.
    19→2. **Architecture changes from v1**:
    20→   - Add temporal self-attention layers before the encoder bottleneck to capture sequential dependencies in trajectory data
    21→   - Increase latent dimension from 32 to 64 to accommodate richer behavioral patterns
    22→   - Replace fixed beta-VAE weighting with cyclical annealing schedule to prevent early latent collapse
    23→3. **Training configuration**: Batch size 256, learning rate 1e-4 with cosine annealing, 100 epochs on the full trajectory dataset. Training executed by the [[lab-agent|lab agent]] on GPU infrastructure.
    24→4. **Evaluation metrics**:
    25→   - Reconstruction MSE (lower is better; target: <0.01 normalized)
    26→   - KL divergence (target: 2.0-8.0 nats; too low = posterior collapse, too high = poor regularization)
    27→   - Latent space interpolation quality (manual inspection of decoded trajectories along latent axes)
    28→   - Downstream task performance: use learned embeddings as features for session outcome prediction
    29→
    30→## Results
    31→
    32→*Experiment in progress. Preliminary results from first 30 epochs:*
    33→
    34→- Reconstruction MSE converging toward 0.015 (vs v1 final: 0.032) -- a 53% improvement in reconstruction quality
    35→- KL divergence stabilized at 4.2 nats after cyclical annealing, indicating a well-regularized latent space without posterior collapse
    36→- Temporal attention layers show clear activation patterns corresponding to tool-switching events and context checkpoint boundaries
    37→- Training throughput: ~3,200 trajectories/second on single GPU, total estimated training time: 4.8 hours for 100 epochs
    38→- Early latent space visualization (t-SNE) shows distinct clusters corresponding to successful vs failed sessions, with a gradient region for partial completions
    39→
    40→## Learnings
    41→
    42→- **Cyclical annealing is essential**: The v1 model suffered from posterior collapse (KL divergence dropped to near-zero in early training). The cyclical annealing schedule from [Fu et al. 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.10145) prevents this by periodically resetting the KL weight, forcing the model to use the latent space.
    43→- **Temporal attention adds value for sequential data**: Treating trajectories as sequences rather than flat vectors improved reconstruction quality significantly. This aligns with [World Models (Ha & Schmidhuber, 2018)](https://worldmodels.github.io/) which demonstrated VAE + recurrent models for learning world representations.
    44→- **Latent dimension sizing**: The increase from 32 to 64 dimensions was justified -- the additional capacity was used (measured by active units metric), not wasted. However, going beyond 64 showed diminishing returns in preliminary sweeps.
    45→- **Data characterization was a prerequisite**: The [[2026-02-24-overnight-simulation-data-characterization-55m-trajectories|55M trajectory characterization]] identified outliers and data quality issues that would have corrupted training without preprocessing.
    46→
    47→## Related
    48→
    49→- [[experience-feedback-loop]] -- VAE training on agent trajectory data closes the experience-to-model feedback loop
    50→- [[structured-experience-vector-layout]] -- experience vectors provide the structured training data for VAE model input
    51→- [[machine-learning]] -- VAE (variational autoencoder) training is a core deep learning technique for latent space compression
    52→- [[machine-learning-optimization]] -- hyperparameter tuning and training schedule optimization for the VAE
    53→- [[neural-network-architecture]] -- the encoder-decoder architecture and attention mechanism design
    54→- [[self-attention-mechanism]] -- temporal self-attention layers added in v2 for sequential trajectory processing
    55→- [[lab-agent]] -- the lab agent executed the training pipeline and collected metrics
    56→- [[compound-engineering]] -- the trained VAE is a compound asset; its embeddings power downstream analytics
    57→
    58→## Primary Sources
    59→
    60→- [Variational Autoencoders (DataCamp Tutorial)](https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/variational-autoencoders) -- comprehensive VAE overview including ELBO derivation
    61→- [VAEs in Reinforcement Learning](https://medium.com/@nicholsonjm92/vaes-in-reinforcement-learning-932fc2df7026) -- survey of VAE applications in RL including World Models
    62→- [Compression of Vehicle Trajectories with a Variational Autoencoder (MDPI)](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/10/19/6739) -- direct precedent for VAE-based trajectory compression
    63→- [VAE+DDPG: Attention-Enhanced VAE for Deep RL Navigation (2025)](https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/aisy.202500636) -- recent work combining VAE with attention for RL agents

     2→title: "Structured Experience Vector Layout"
     3→date: "2026-02-23"
     4→tags: [pattern]
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Problem
     8→
     9→Reinforcement learning experience replay requires storing (state, action, reward, next_state, done) tuples. When the agent state is a high-dimensional structured vector, naive concatenation creates experience vectors that are hard to inspect, debug, and consume correctly in training.
    10→
    11→## Solution
    12→
    13→Define an experience vector as a structured concatenation with explicit named offsets. Provide accessors that slice the experience vector back into its components without requiring callers to remember offsets.
    14→
    15→An experience record contains:
    16→- **current_state**: agent state at time t (D_state features)
    17→- **action_embedding**: embedding of the action taken (D_action features)
    18→- **reward**: scalar reward, normalized (1 feature)
    19→- **next_state**: agent state at time t+1 (D_state features)
    20→- **done**: episode termination flag (1 feature)
    21→- **metadata**: step count, episode ID, agent ID (M features)
    22→
    23→## Code Example
    24→
    25→```python
    26→import numpy as np
    27→from typing import ClassVar, NamedTuple
    28→
    29→class ExperienceVector:
    30→    """Structured experience vector for FLUME agent training.
    31→
    32→    Layout: [current_state | action_embedding | reward | next_state | done | metadata]
    33→    """
    34→    STATE_DIM: ClassVar[int] = 64
    35→    ACTION_DIM: ClassVar[int] = 16
    36→    META_DIM: ClassVar[int] = 4
    37→    TOTAL_DIM: ClassVar[int] = 64 + 16 + 1 + 64 + 1 + 4  # = 150
    38→
    39→    # Segment slices
    40→    CURRENT_STATE: ClassVar[slice] = slice(0, 64)
    41→    ACTION: ClassVar[slice] = slice(64, 80)
    42→    REWARD: ClassVar[int] = 80
    43→    NEXT_STATE: ClassVar[slice] = slice(81, 145)
    44→    DONE: ClassVar[int] = 145
    45→    META: ClassVar[slice] = slice(146, 150)
    46→
    47→    def __init__(self, current_state, action_embedding, reward, next_state, done, metadata=None):
    48→        self._vec = np.zeros(self.TOTAL_DIM, dtype=np.float32)
    49→        self._vec[self.CURRENT_STATE] = current_state
    50→        self._vec[self.ACTION] = action_embedding
    51→        self._vec[self.REWARD] = reward
    52→        self._vec[self.NEXT_STATE] = next_state
    53→        self._vec[self.DONE] = float(done)
    54→        if metadata is not None:
    55→            self._vec[self.META] = metadata
    56→
    57→    @classmethod
    58→    def from_vec(cls, vec: np.ndarray) -> 'ExperienceVector':
    59→        obj = cls.__new__(cls)
    60→        obj._vec = vec
    61→        return obj
    62→
    63→    def get_current_state(self) -> np.ndarray:
    64→        return self._vec[self.CURRENT_STATE]
    65→
    66→    def get_action(self) -> np.ndarray:
    67→        return self._vec[self.ACTION]
    68→
    69→    def get_reward(self) -> float:
    70→        return float(self._vec[self.REWARD])
    71→
    72→    def get_next_state(self) -> np.ndarray:
    73→        return self._vec[self.NEXT_STATE]
    74→
    75→    def is_done(self) -> bool:
    76→        return bool(self._vec[self.DONE])
    77→
    78→    def to_numpy(self) -> np.ndarray:
    79→        return self._vec
    80→```
    81→
    82→## When to Use
    83→
    84→- Building replay buffers for agent training
    85→- Logging experiences for offline analysis or FLUME training data collection
    86→- Any pipeline where (s, a, r, s', done) needs to be stored and retrieved efficiently as numpy arrays
    87→
    88→**Storage**: Store as float32 numpy arrays in a pre-allocated ring buffer. For 150-dimensional experiences, 1M experiences = ~600 MB. The flat numpy format allows efficient batch sampling with `buffer[indices]`.
    89→
    90→## Related
    91→
    92→- [[structured-feature-vector-layout-for-agent-state]]
    93→- [[vae-checkpoint-format-with-config]]
    94→- [[machine-learning]] — experience vectors serve as training data for reinforcement learning and VAE models
    95→- [[agent-journey-tracking]] — journey tracking produces the state observations that become experience vector components
    96→- [[experience-feedback-loop]] — structured experience vectors are the data format that closes the feedback loop from execution to training
    97→- [[2026-02-24-flume-vae-v2-training-results]] — FLUME VAE v2 training consumes these structured experience vectors as input data
    98→- [[neural-network-architecture]] — the vector layout (state/action/reward/next_state/done) follows standard neural network RL training data conventions
    99→

     7→
     8→# 12D Manifold
     9→
    10→The 12-dimensional manifold is the mathematical space underlying the Cohezion vault's hyperdimensional visualization system. Each vault note is represented as a point in this 12D space, where each dimension encodes a distinct semantic property of the note. The [[12D-Projection]] system then projects this high-dimensional representation down to 3D for interactive visualization.
    11→
    12→## Definition
    13→
    14→A manifold is a topological space that locally resembles Euclidean space. The 12D Manifold in Cohezion is a 12-dimensional real-valued space where each dimension corresponds to one of the vault's semantic scoring dimensions. Every note in the vault occupies a position in this space determined by its properties, and the distances between points encode semantic similarity.
    15→
    16→## The 12 Dimensions
    17→
    18→The Cohezion 3D graph plugin computes 8 primary semantic dimensions, with 4 additional derived dimensions:
    19→
    20→### Primary Dimensions
    21→1. **Connectivity** — number of inbound and outbound wiki-links (graph degree)
    22→2. **Conceptual Depth** — richness of content (word count, section count, frontmatter completeness)
    23→3. **Temporal Distribution** — how the note's references span across time periods
    24→4. **Cross-Domain Presence** — number of distinct tag domains the note connects to
    25→5. **Completion Maturity** — status progression (stub -> active -> complete)
    26→6. **Recency** — time since last modification, weighted by activity patterns
    27→7. **Semantic Similarity** — embedding-based similarity to neighboring notes (via Ollama)
    28→8. **Domain Clustering** — membership in topic clusters derived from tag co-occurrence
    29→
    30→### Derived Dimensions (9-12)
    31→9. **Bridge Score** — betweenness centrality in the wiki-link graph
    32→10. **Velocity** — rate of change in connectivity over recent sessions
    33→11. **Influence Radius** — how many notes are reachable within 2 hops
    34→12. **Coherence** — consistency of the note's topic with its linked neighbors
    35→
    36→## Key Properties
    37→
    38→- **Continuous:** Each dimension is a real-valued score, not categorical, enabling smooth interpolation between notes
    39→- **Normalized:** All dimensions are scaled to [0, 1] to prevent any single dimension from dominating distance calculations
    40→- **Updateable:** Dimension scores are recomputed after each vault modification, making the manifold a living representation of vault state
    41→- **Projectable:** The 12D space is reduced to 3D via t-SNE or UMAP-like projection for the [[force-directed-graph]] visualization
    42→
    43→## Sources
    44→
    45→- Internal Cohezion architecture — the 12D Manifold was designed as part of the 3D graph plugin
    46→- [t-SNE: Visualizing High-Dimensional Data (van der Maaten & Hinton)](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v9/vandermaaten08a.html)
    47→
    48→## Related
    49→
    50→- [[12D-Projection]] — the projection system that maps 12D manifold positions to 3D screen coordinates
    51→- [[force-directed-graph]] — the 3D visualization uses force-directed layout after projection from 12D
    52→- [[knowledge-graph-systems]] — the manifold is computed from the vault's knowledge graph structure
    53→- [[semantic-search]] — semantic similarity (dimension 7) uses the same embeddings as vault search
    54→- [[compound-engineering]] — the manifold provides a quantitative view of vault health for compound engineering sprints
    55→- [[knowledge-graph-densification]] — densification changes manifold positions by increasing connectivity dimensions
    56→
    57→## Daily References
    58→

    60→- [[2026-02-09-3d-graph-plugin-installation-complete]] — 3D Graph plugin v2.4.1 installed and configured for 12D visualization
    61→- [[2026-02-10-phase1-complete]] — Phase 1 complete: 5 computational dimensions implemented
    62→- [[2026-02-10-phase2-kickoff]] — Phase 2 kickoff: semantic dimensions via Ollama
    63→- [[2026-02-10-phase2-semantic-dimensions-complete]] — Phase 2 complete: semantic dimensions via Ollama in 8K tokens
    64→- [[2026-02-10-phase3-kickoff]] — Phase 3 kickoff: 3D graph visualization
    65→- [[2026-02-10-phase3-progress]] — Phase 3 progress: tasks 1-2 complete, plugin specialist active
    66→- [[2026-02-10-phase3b-plugin-ready]] — Phase 3b: 3D graph plugin installed and ready for dimensional data
    67→- [[2026-02-10-phase3-complete]] — Phase 3 complete: 12D graph visualization ready in 1 day vs 1 week planned
    68→
    69→## Relevance to Cohezion
    70→
    71→The 12D Manifold is the quantitative foundation for the Cohezion vault's visualization and analytics capabilities. By encoding multiple semantic properties as dimensions, it enables the 3D graph plugin to cluster related notes, highlight bridges between topic domains, and visually identify thin or disconnected areas of the knowledge graph that need attention during compound engineering sprints.

     8→
     9→# Triage Inbox Notes
    10→
    11→Process notes from `inbox/` into their permanent homes — researching topics, adding structure, applying frontmatter, and creating cross-links.
    12→
    13→## Usage
    14→
    15→```
    16→/triage [options]
    17→```
    18→
    19→- `/triage` — Process all inbox notes
    20→- `/triage inbox/note-name.md` — Process a specific note
    21→- `/triage --dry-run` — Show what would happen without making changes
    22→
    23→## Execution Steps
    24→
    25→### 1. Scan Inbox
    26→
    27→```bash
    28→ls -la inbox/*.md 2>/dev/null
    29→```
    30→
    31→List all notes with their sizes. Skip non-markdown files.
    32→
    33→### 2. For Each Note, Classify
    34→
    35→Read the note content and determine:
    36→
    37→| Classification | Target Directory | Criteria |
    38→|---------------|-----------------|----------|
    39→| **Concept** | `concepts/` | Defines a term, idea, or technology |
    40→| **Paper/Research** | `papers/` | Summarizes research, findings, or external source |
    41→| **Decision** | `decisions/` | Records an architectural or strategic choice |
    42→| **Pattern** | `patterns/` | Describes a reusable solution to a problem |
    43→| **Experiment** | `experiments/` | Documents a hypothesis test or trial |
    44→| **Project** | `projects/` | Tracks ongoing work or initiative |
    45→| **Discard** | (delete) | Empty, duplicate, or no longer relevant |
    46→
    47→If classification is ambiguous, ask the user.
    48→
    49→### 3. Research and Expand
    50→
    51→For each note being triaged:
    52→
    53→1. **Read existing content** — Understand what the user captured
    54→2. **Research the topic** — Use WebSearch to find authoritative information
    55→3. **Write structured content** following the target directory's template:
    56→   - Concepts: Definition, Key Properties, Examples, Related
    57→   - Papers: Summary, Key Findings, Methodology, Implications
    58→   - Decisions: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives
    59→   - Patterns: Problem, Solution, Code Example, When to Use
    60→4. **Preserve user's original notes** — Incorporate their observations, don't overwrite
    61→5. **Add Primary Sources** — Include real URLs from research
    62→
    63→### 4. Build Frontmatter
    64→
    65→Apply the target directory's required fields:
    66→
    67→```yaml
    68→---
    69→title: "Properly Cased Title"
    70→date: YYYY-MM-DD  # use original date if present, otherwise today
    71→status: active    # for decisions/experiments/projects
    72→tags: [type-tag, domain-tag1, domain-tag2]
    73→related_concepts: [concept1, concept2]  # for concept notes
    74→---
    75→```
    76→
    77→**Tag rules:**
    78→- Check existing vault tags first: `grep -roh 'tags: \[.*\]' concepts/ papers/ | sort -u`
    79→- Reuse established tags where possible
    80→- Tags must be YAML arrays
    81→
    82→### 5. Generate Filename
    83→
    84→- Slugify the title: lowercase, hyphens, no special chars
    85→- Add date prefix for temporal notes (decisions, experiments, projects)
    86→- Check for filename collisions
    87→
    88→### 6. Find and Add Links
    89→
    90→Before moving the note:
    91→
    92→1. Search vault for related notes by topic/tags
    93→2. Add `[[wiki-links]]` to Related sections in the new note
    94→3. Add backlinks in related notes pointing to the new note
    95→
    96→### 7. Move the Note
    97→
    98→1. Write the structured note to the target directory
    99→2. Delete the original from `inbox/`
   100→3. Verify the file exists in its new location
   101→
   102→### 8. Report
   103→
   104→```markdown
   105→## Triage Report
   106→
   107→| Inbox Note | Action | Destination | Links Added |
   108→|------------|--------|-------------|-------------|
   109→| note-1.md | Moved | concepts/topic.md | 4 |
   110→| note-2.md | Moved | papers/research.md | 3 |
   111→| note-3.md | Discarded | — | — |
   112→
   113→**Processed:** X notes
   114→**Moved:** Y notes
   115→**Discarded:** Z notes
   116→**Links created:** N bidirectional pairs
   117→```
   118→
   119→## Batch Processing
   120→
   121→When processing multiple inbox notes:
   122→
   123→1. Classify all notes first (show the plan)
   124→2. Process in order: concepts first (they're link targets), then papers, then decisions
   125→3. This ordering maximizes bidirectional linking opportunities
   126→
   127→## Quality Checks
   128→
   129→Before marking triage complete:
   130→
   131→- [ ] All frontmatter is valid YAML with array tags
   132→- [ ] No duplicate notes in target directory
   133→- [ ] At least 2-3 wiki-links added per note
   134→- [ ] Content is substantive (not just a stub)
   135→- [ ] Original inbox note is deleted
   136→- [ ] Backlinks added in related notes
   137→
   138→## Notes
   139→
   140→- Preserve the user's original insight/observation — it's the seed
   141→- Research supplements the user's note, doesn't replace it
   142→- If a note is too vague to classify, ask the user before guessing
   143→- Empty inbox notes (just a title) should be treated as concept stubs — research and expand
   144→- The goal is zero inbox — all notes processed and properly filed
   145→

     8→
     9→# Create Vault Note
    10→
    11→Create a new note in the correct vault directory with proper frontmatter, structure, and bidirectional wiki-links.
    12→
    13→## Usage
    14→
    15→```
    16→/note <type> <title> [description]
    17→```
    18→
    19→**Types:** `concept`, `paper`, `decision`, `pattern`, `experiment`, `project`, `inbox`
    20→
    21→**Examples:**
    22→- `/note concept reinforcement learning`
    23→- `/note decision switch from REST to GraphQL`
    24→- `/note paper new quantum computing breakthrough`
    25→- `/note pattern retry-with-backoff`
    26→
    27→## Execution Steps
    28→
    29→### 1. Determine Directory and Template
    30→
    31→| Type | Directory | Date Prefix | Required Fields |
    32→|------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
    33→| concept | `concepts/` | No | title, date, tags |
    34→| paper | `papers/` | No | title, date, tags |
    35→| decision | `decisions/` | Yes (`YYYY-MM-DD-`) | title, date, status, tags |
    36→| pattern | `patterns/` | No | title, date, tags |
    37→| experiment | `experiments/` | Yes (`YYYY-MM-DD-`) | title, date, status, tags |
    38→| project | `projects/` | Yes (`YYYY-MM-DD-`) | title, date, status, tags |
    39→| inbox | `inbox/` | Yes (`YYYY-MM-DD-`) | title, date |
    40→
    41→### 2. Generate Filename
    42→
    43→- Slugify the title: lowercase, hyphens for spaces, remove special chars
    44→- Add date prefix where required: `YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md`
    45→- Check for duplicates before creating
    46→
    47→### 3. Check for Existing Notes
    48→
    49→Before creating, search for existing notes on the same topic:
    50→
    51→```bash
    52→# Search by filename similarity
    53→find concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ -name "*keyword*" -type f
    54→
    55→# Search by content
    56→grep -rl "keyword" concepts/ papers/ decisions/ patterns/ 2>/dev/null
    57→```
    58→
    59→If duplicates exist, warn the user and suggest linking instead.
    60→
    61→### 4. Build Frontmatter
    62→
    63→Use the directory's required fields. Tags MUST be arrays:
    64→
    65→```yaml
    66→---
    67→title: "Note Title"
    68→date: YYYY-MM-DD
    69→status: proposed  # only for decisions, experiments, projects
    70→tags: [tag1, tag2, tag3]
    71→related_concepts: [concept1, concept2]  # for concepts
    72→---
    73→```
    74→
    75→**Tag guidelines:**
    76→- Use existing vault tags where possible (check other notes in same directory)
    77→- Include the type tag (e.g., `concept`, `decision`, `pattern`)
    78→- Add 2-4 domain tags from the note's subject matter
    79→- Use lowercase, hyphenated multi-word tags
    80→
    81→### 5. Build Content Structure
    82→
    83→**Concept notes:**
    84→```markdown
    85→## Definition
    86→[Clear, concise definition — 2-3 sentences]
    87→
    88→## Key Properties
    89→- [Property 1]
    90→- [Property 2]
    91→
    92→## Examples
    93→- [Concrete example 1]
    94→- [Concrete example 2]
    95→
    96→## Related Papers
    97→- [[paper-name]]
    98→
    99→## Related Concepts
   100→- [[concept-name]]
   101→
   102→## Relevance to Cohezion
   103→[How this concept connects to the Cohezion framework]
   104→```
   105→
   106→**Decision notes (ADR format):**
   107→```markdown
   108→## Context
   109→[What prompted this decision]
   110→
   111→## Decision
   112→[What was decided]
   113→
   114→## Consequences
   115→[What follows from this decision]
   116→
   117→## Alternatives Considered
   118→[What else was evaluated]
   119→```
   120→
   121→**Pattern notes:**
   122→```markdown
   123→## Problem
   124→[What problem does this solve]
   125→
   126→## Solution
   127→[The reusable approach]
   128→
   129→## Code Example
   130→[Implementation with code block]
   131→
   132→## When to Use
   133→[Applicability guidelines]
   134→
   135→## When NOT to Use
   136→[Counter-indications]
   137→```
   138→
   139→**Paper notes:**
   140→```markdown
   141→## Summary
   142→[2-3 sentence summary of the paper/finding]
   143→
   144→## Key Findings
   145→- [Finding 1]
   146→- [Finding 2]
   147→
   148→## Methodology
   149→[How the research was conducted]
   150→
   151→## Implications
   152→[Why this matters]
   153→
   154→## Related Papers
   155→- [[related-paper]]
   156→
   157→## Related Concepts
   158→- [[related-concept]]
   159→```
   160→
   161→### 6. Add Bidirectional Links
   162→
   163→After creating the note:
   164→
   165→1. Identify 3-5 existing notes that relate to this topic
   166→2. Add `[[wiki-links]]` in the new note's Related sections
   167→3. Add a backlink `[[new-note]]` in each related note's Related section
   168→
   169→This maintains the vault's bidirectional linking convention.
   170→
   171→### 7. Research Content (When Requested)
   172→
   173→If the user provides a topic but no content:
   174→
   175→1. Use WebSearch to find authoritative information
   176→2. Use Context7 if the topic relates to a library/framework
   177→3. Write structured content following the template
   178→4. Include Primary Sources section with real URLs
   179→5. Never fabricate citations — only include sources you actually found
   180→
   181→### 8. Verify
   182→
   183→- Frontmatter is valid YAML
   184→- Tags are arrays
   185→- Wiki-links point to existing notes (or flag as new stubs)
   186→- File is in the correct directory
   187→- No duplicate notes exist
   188→
   189→## Notes
   190→
   191→- Always check for existing notes before creating new ones
   192→- Prefer linking to existing notes over creating duplicates
   193→- When creating concept stubs for links, use the minimal concept template
   194→- Today's date for the `date` field: use current date from system
   195→
